The study’s conclusions have been drawn through a close reading of a selected play; a thorough examination of the political and social tensions during the time of publication; as well as from a real sense of the gripping cultural atmosphere of Harlem, gained through a recent visit.

title: Reading in Borges and Benjamin
abstract: Jorge Luis Borges and Walter Benjamin have come to be seen as two of the most important writers of the 20th century: Borges in fiction and Benjamin in the realm of literary criticism. Two questions immediately present themselves for a study of the two: how and why should they be read together? As facile as it may seem, I suggest that reading their own techniques of reading is a useful way to consider them. Benjamin is in almost every respect a more serious writer than Borges. The urgency of his own historical situation—1930s Germany—is palpable in his writings, which are motivated by a consideration of history that brings the present into a crisis. Borges’ literary works, on the other hand, do not respond to any sort of critical situation. They are rather a product of his reading: he dedicated his life to reading (and re-reading) as much as possible. Looking at reading in the two writers thus puts Borges on equal footing with Benjamin. I focus a reading of Benjamin on texts where he submits books and libraries to his critical procedure. What emerges from these writings is that Benjamin’s conception of reading is not all that dissimilar from Borges’. Each writer, for example, is interested by the possibilities of collecting books, and the fate of each particular book in a collection. Their reading techniques, in fact, illuminate each other’s writings: an understanding of Borges and Benjamin in this way has not yet been attempted.

title: The Role of Race in Public Opinion of American Governmental Policies
abstract: Are Americans’ political ideologies and endorsements of government policies toward African-Americans influenced by racism and prejudice? This question is a constant fixture in American policy discourse. While numerous sociological, political, and psychological theories debate this problem, there is still the question of whether or not racial prejudice drives individual’s attitudes and government policy preferences. A new field has recently developed that applies subconscious measurements (implicit attitudes) and these measurements have shown to be a predictor of individual’s behavior towards members of the group s/he has implicit bias against (Dovidio, Kawakami, & Gaertner 2002; Fazio et al. 1995; Greenwald et al. 1998; Payne et al. 2005). Applying regression analyses, my research examines leading theories in the fields of sociology, political-sociology, psychology, and two forms of implicit attitude measurement (Implicit Attitude Test, Affect Misattribution Procedure), along with surveys addressing current government policy, to determine whether or not there were any relationships between or among the variables. These different variables have never been tested together to determine interactions or correlates. Results indicated that the theory of Symbolic Racism, above and beyond any other variable, most aptly described the trends of resistance of white Americans’ public opinion regarding government policies directed towards African Americans.

title: Sana, Sana Colita de Rana: A Generational Study of Contemporary Counterborder Curanderismo
abstract: This project offers a generational perspectives of curanderismo, the Mexican system of traditional healing which addresses illnesses of the body, mind, and spirit, in a Mexican American family in Chicago and contemporary counterborder curanderismo. Here counterborder makes reference to the spatially fluid and ever changing state of curanderismo. More importantly, it addresses the lack of a static, solid, or distinct border between the practice of curanderismo in Mexico and in Chicago. A counterborder perspective is important in the study of contemporary curanderismo whose practical day to day use is rooted in the ‘traditional’ form but has developed into an ‘updated’ version for a newer community in a newer setting. Ethnographic fieldwork included interviews and participant observation and took place in Apipilulco and Iguala, Guerrero, Mexico and throughout the city of Chicago. Data was divided into the generational groups studied in order to aid in the analysis. As a result, this generational study invites the visualization of the tradition through an artistic medium to incite the study of culture through contemporary art. Through video and installation, audiences are exposed to curanderismo and build a personal relationship to it. Moreover, they share the artist’s role as insider/outsider, colonized/colonizer, and academic/artist. The inclusion of contemporary art also facilitates the discussion of a contemporary counterborder curanderismo through the medium of the visual arts.

title: Paganism and Pessimism in the Novels of Thomas Hardy
abstract: To what can we attribute Thomas Hardy's misery, his disheartened assessment of man, and, as one scholar of Hardy, Ruth Firor has remarked, his "brooding pity for all living things"? Traditional scholarship stresses the tragic vision of Hardy's works: the author's profound melancholy and grim resignation fascinate readers as subjects for intellectual inquiry. If we come to understand Hardy through his personal memoranda as well as his novels, we can better explain the vast implication of his religious philosophy against the backdrop of Victorian England. My research explores the degree and manner in which Hardy extracts a religious sensibility from ancient ritual, and whether that sensibility allows his characters to live and die with integrity. I argue that Hardy documents the survival of an older, Pagan era that had its basis in dependence on the earth, not on god; his novels explore Paganism as an alternative to the dogma of institutional Christianity. For the project, I studied relevant texts at Oxford University's Bodleian Library and visited Dorset (the birthplace of Hardy) and the Dorset County Museum, where many of Hardy's original manuscripts are held. This spring, I also worked at the Beinecke Library at Yale University and examined Hardy's private collection of novels and essays.

title: Traditional Ecological Knowledge, Acculturation, and Child Health Among the Tsimane’ of Lowland Bolivia
abstract: The project examines the associations between traditional ecological knowledge (TEK), acculturation, and child health in an indigenous population in the Bolivian Amazon. Traditional ecological knowledge, the knowledge of wild plant species and their uses, is universal to indigenous cultures; recent studies are revealing its significance for health, as well as other issues. The effect of acculturation on health is still ambiguous, as is the effect of acculturation on TEK. The research population, the Tsimane’, was relatively isolated until the 1950s, but for past several decades has become increasingly integrated into a market economy. However, the Tsimane’ (who number about 8,000 and live in over 100 villages) have acculturated at different paces and in different ways; additionally, their location in an area noted for its botanical diversity make the Tsimane’ good subjects for this study. Previous work has examined the distribution of TEK among the Tsimane’ and the culturally relative value of specific plants, but TEK has not yet been studied in relation to child health. Results indicate that traditional ecological knowledge is beneficial for child health, especially for malnourished children. The impact of acculturation on health is small but generally negative; TEK is negatively associated with parental acculturation. This study highlights the importance of TEK for child health as well as the threat to TEK from acculturation. Future policies should recognize the importance of TEK and try to protect it from degradation.

title: The Cultural Double Standard: Understanding Perceptions of Infanticide in Nineteenth-Century Great Britain and India
abstract: In the early nineteenth century, infanticide remained prevalent in Great Britain. The typical accused woman was a young, poor single mother. Though the official penalty for infanticide was the death penalty, juries were often reluctant to convict; many were excused on the grounds of temporary insanity. In the same period, officials of British East India Company and English missionaries were soon enacting invasive policies to prevent the practice in India. The British took an avid interest in controlling infanticide because it provided a way to establish local authority in areas otherwise outside their political control by disrupting marriage patterns that perpetuated hierarchies among the Indian elite. The British colonials were horrified by female infanticide practices of the elite castes, which they attributed to exorbitantly high dowry costs. How could the British adopt an indifferent attitude toward infanticide in Britain, continuing to acquit accused mothers in Great Britain (without acknowledging the circumstances leading to her crime) while at the same time strive to suppress the practice in India? The historian Satadru Sen argues that the British seized upon the moral opprobrium attracted to female infanticide to further their colonial ambitions in India, and my research expands upon this argument to compare British colonial perceptions of Indian infanticide with the prevalence of infanticide among British mothers. I suggest that infanticide became entirely embedded in the British cultural double standard of the implicit tolerance of the practice among poor women destroying their illegitimate children in Great Britain, but condemning the practice of the elite married couple murdering their female children in India.

title: Synthesis and Characterization of Silica Aerogel for Use In Superfluid 3He Experiments
abstract: Silica aerogels are a form of highly porous glass (~98% porosity) that can be used to introduce impurities into superfluid 3He. It has been speculated that new superfluid phases of 3He might be stabilized inside of anisotropic silica aerogels. To this end, we established a facility at Northwestern to produce both isotropic and anisotropic aerogels for use in the study of superfluid 3He. We found that highly isotropic aerogels can be chemically synthesized by a process that includes solvent exchange followed by a slow and even temperature ramp during the supercritical removal of this solvent. Anisotropy can then be introduced into these samples via compression. In addition, we have found that samples that shrink during the synthesis process exhibit intrinsic anisotropy. We have measured the degree of anisotropy in our samples using Small Angle X-ray Scattering (SAXS). These characterized samples are now being used to study the effect of anisotropy on the phases of superfluid 3He. The next goal of our group is to produce even higher porosity (≥ 99%) aerogels to explore how the 3He system transitions from the pure to the impure state.

title: Floating-Point Emulation for Fault Tolerance and Reliability
abstract: The decreasing size of transistors found in modern microprocessors has led to an increasing number of chips lost to manufacturing defects and in-operation failures, resulting in increased cost due to failed parts and a reduction in processor lifetime. A common technique for mitigating these effects is duplication of selected hardware, providing a layer of redundancy in the event of a failure. While this has proven to be effective for hardware components with regular structures, such as caches, it cannot be applied to components such as arithmetic logic units (ALUs), which consist of a heterogeneous set of smaller components. To provide redundancy for these components, the entire unit must be duplicated, which can be very inefficient. An alternative solution is to utilize existing hardware to emulate the instructions that are dependent upon a failed resource. Floating-point arithmetic operations, which require a separate ALU, are particularly well suited for emulation, as they can be readily represented as sequence of integer arithmetic operations, which do not utilize floating-point hardware. The implementation presented here uses a virtual machine monitor (VMM) to detect failures. When a failure is detected, execution of instructions affected by the failure causes the processor to execute the stored emulation routines, computing the correct result without requiring the use of the hardware affected by the failure. In all, instruction emulation can be used to make microprocessors more tolerant of both in-operation faults and manufacturing defects, which translates into longer device lifetime and a potential reduction in cost.

title: From Faithfulness to Factuality: Semantic Change in the English Vocabulary of Truth
abstract: The semantic change of English words relating to truth form a cognitive vocabulary varying between the moral and the epistemic. While true originally referred to one’s faithfulness and loyalty, true now also defines a statement or belief that is factual, consistent with reality. A corpus study documenting this change across the Old through Early Modern English periods yields an explanatory account based on: 1) mechanisms of semantic change and 2) motivations for the change provided by a social model of language contact. The semantic change of true words demonstrates two hypothesized trends: a pattern from deontic to epistemic meaning as well as a correlating rise of subjectivity (Traugott 1989). The original faithfulness meaning of true corresponds with deontic meanings of obligation, while the later meanings of factuality invite a more epistemic sense of knowledge and beliefs. The Invited Inferencing Theory (Traugott and Dasher 2002) models this change, as speakers draw on pragmatic meanings that get negotiated through conventionalizing implicatures and thus spark change. An examination of the dates and frequencies of this particular semantic change shows the likelihood for French influence as a contributor towards that process. Indeed, English and French contact was a mixture of primarily borrowing with minimal shift-induced interference. Contact with French provided new lexical choices (such as loyal and faithful) for describing the original sense of true. Combining models of contact with acquisition, the anti-synonymy constraint (in which new words mean new things) helps explain why increased use of the French words corresponded with the increasing use of the new meanings for true.

title: Empirical Evidence for Existence of 3D-Photonic Nanojet
abstract: The diffraction limit of light restricts the use of the visible spectrum to image sub nanometer sized samples. Current methods for imaging sub-diffractional objects include Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM), and Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM), but these instruments are often incompatible and highly tedious in their application to many biological samples. However, recent FDTD simulations have shown that dielectric spheres on the order of the wavelength of the electromagnetic spectrum are capable of producing a region of high intensity radiation on the sphere’s shadow side: a phenomenon called the 3D-Photonic Nanojet. Furthermore, simulations have shown that placing an object within this high-intensity region produces a significant enhancement in backscattering through the sphere. One application of this technology is imaging sub-diffractional samples using visible light. Until recently, the existence of the 3D-photonic Nanojet has been purely theoretical. Over the past several months, we have employed various chemical and optical techniques to observe empirically this phenomenon. These techniques include microsphere coupling using biotin-streptavidin protein-protein interactions and more recently, nanofabrication, using Quanta SEM.

title: Conversion and Islamic Mysticism in The Autobiography of Malcolm X
abstract: Malcolm X, one of America’s “most outspoken revolutionaries,” is famous for his sharp rhetoric, leadership in the Black Revolution, and dedication to civil and human rights. Most scholarship on Malcolm X addresses his political and racial ideas; the sparse religious scholarship examines his leadership in the Black Muslim movement and his outward demonstration of religiosity through a sectarian lens. The project takes a bold step away from the existing literature by approaching The Autobiography of Malcolm X through a lens of his conversion to Islam. Research focused on Malcolm’s two prominent spiritual experiences: his conversion in prison and his pilgrimage to Mecca (Hajj). While these events are typically considered two separate conversions (to the Nation of Islam and Sunni Islam), my analysis asserts their fundamental continuity. The prison conversion can be likened to the spiritual experience of withdrawal, retreat from worldly distraction into pure contemplation of God. Malcolm’s conversion in prison echoes the Prophet Muhammad’s withdrawal into Cave Hira, where he received the First Revelations (Qur’an). Years later, the Hajj witnessed the culmination of Malcolm’s conversion. In gathering, Malcolm experienced the unity of creation (brotherhood of man) as a reflection of the unity of God. Despite the apparent diversity of creation, there is an underlying unity that reflects the unified nature of its Creator. The deepest significance of Malcolm’s withdrawal and gathering, then, attests to the same reality: the unity of God. Prison and Hajj therefore represent two faces of Malcolm’s singular conversion experience.

title: Brainstem Responses and Their Relationship to Cortical Encoding of Speech Sounds
abstract: Previous studies have shown an abundance of speech-evoked brainstem and cortical deficits in learning disabled (LD) children, but with much less attention given to the relationship between them. In this study, we investigated whether speech-evoked brainstem timing delays, evident in roughly 30% of LD children predict cortical response abnormalities to speech syllables. Our hypothesis is that speech encoding proceeds from peripheral to central neural structures and that deficits at lower levels (i.e. the brainstem) influence higher level responses (i.e. the cortex). The LD children were further divided into 2 subgroups: LDd (LD with delayed brainstem timing) and LDn (LD with normal brainstem timing). Preliminary results using point to point t-test scores across group grand average waveforms of normal learners (NL), LDd, and LDn children have shown that children with a delayed brainstem timing may also have poor cortical timing (characterized by a reduced P1/N1b slope). Additionally, as a group, only LDn have shown a different representation of /da/ vs. /ga/ stimuli. In conclusion, these findings suggest that delayed brainstem timing is related to an overall cortical encoding deficit, regardless of any difference between the speech stimuli /da/ and /ga/. Also, that LDn have cortical encoding deficits that are unique from those observed in their LDd counterparts.

title: Preparation of a Graphite NanocompositeUsing Ring-Opening Metathesis Polymerization
abstract: In recent years, polymer nanocomposites have attracted a great deal of interests as a new generation of strong, lightweight materials that may revolutionize the transportation, construction, and sport industries in the same manner that polymers ushered in the plastic age in the mid 1900’s. Critical to the enhanced mechanical properties of these nanocomposites are the particle shape and size, the surface characteristics, and the degree of dispersion of the selected nanofiller components inside polymer matrices. Given these criteria, graphene nanoplatelets, the structural unit of graphite and single wall carbon nanotubes, are predicted to be excellent nanofiller components due to their remarkable in-plane mechanical, electrical, and thermal properties. In an effort to create a homogenous graphite-polymer nanocomposite, we attempted to covalently grow monodisperse polymer chains from both graphite oxide (GO) and thermally expanded graphite oxide (TEGO) using ring-opening metathesis polymerization (ROMP). Ammonium-salt-based precursors to ROMP initiators were synthesized and successfully intercalated between layers of GO as evidenced by IR spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, and elemental analysis. We also attempted to attach Grubbs 1st-generation ROMP catalyst to these intercalated initiator precursors. However, subsequent ROMP experiments failed to yield polymer nanocomposites, most likely because Grubbs catalyst, a relatively bulky molecule, could not intercalate between the GO layers. TEGO was then substituted as source of graphene nanoplatelets since the distance between each graphene layer in this material was greatly increased in comparison to GO, allowing for incorporation of Grubbs catalyst. A pyrene-based ROMP initiator precursor was first bound to the TEGO surface through van der Waals interactions. Subsequent attachment of Grubbs 1st-generation ROMP catalyst to the pyrene derivative was then attempted followed by ROMP reaction with cis-cyclooctene. While monodisperse polymers could be formed readily, they are cleaved from the TEGO surface quite easily, most likely because the bonds between the pyrene initiator and the TEGO surface were weak, and no nanocomposites could be isolated.

title: 14-month-olds’ interpretations of nouns and adjectives
abstract: Language development research is fundamental to our understanding of how infants perceive the world and, more specifically, how they establish relations between words and objects. Infants gradually begin to make connections between words and their referents during their first year. Distinct words, such as nouns and adjectives, can highlight distinct aspects of the same object, such as the category to which it belongs (e.g., animal, vehicle, dog) and the properties that it possesses (e.g., big, fast, red), respectively. Previous research has shown that 14-month-old infants correctly map novel nouns specifically to categories of objects, whereas they have more general expectations about adjectives, mapping them to both categories and properties of objects. This data was based on an interactive task (where an experimenter presents the materials). We have now developed a new automated task (presented as a video) to assess whether the same results can be attained using a comparable procedure. We predicted that 14-month-olds who participated in the new procedure would reveal the same results as in the interactive procedure. Three experiments were developed with the automated procedure to test this prediction. Results revealed that 14-month-old infants do in fact reflect the same behavior as they did in the previously conducted study (Experiments 1 and 2). Moreover, results showed that 18-month-olds who participated in the automated procedure maintain the notion that nouns refer to object categories, and have begun to map adjectives specifically to properties of objects (Experiment 3).

title: Drug Toxicity and Adverse Side Effects in Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD): Effect of Proton Pump Inhibitors (PPIs) on Gastrointestinal Flora
abstract: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), such as Protonix, are given to patients to counter the effects of gastroesophageal reflux disease by shutting down proton pumps, thereby increasing the pH of the stomach. It is known that certain strains of bacteria colonizing the oral cavity and upper gastrointestinal tract have proton pumps similar in structure to human proton pumps. This DNA homology suggests that PPIs may also affect the activity of prokaryotic proton pumps. For this experiment, nineteen strains of Lactobacilli were inoculated in microtiter plates in media at a pH of 4.5, 5.0, or 5.5, depending on the sensitivity of the bacteria, with two-fold dilutions of Protonix at a range of 2.5 mg/mL to 2.5 μg/mL. Bacterial growth was monitored and the minimal inhibitory concentration (MIC) of the drug was determined. In cases where growth was inhibited, Gram-staining was carried out to visualize any potential morphological changes in the bacteria. Furthermore, growth curves were obtained to determine if growth was impeded at pharmacological doses of Protonix. Eight of the nineteen Lactobacilli strains were found to have an MIC below 313 µg/mL. Additionally, Gram-staining of certain strains, such as L. s. salivarius 11741, revealed conformational changes in the bacteria grown in the presence of Protonix. Growth curves at pharmacological doses demonstrated inhibited growth of certain strains. Thus, the slowed growth and conformational changes observed in a number of strains in the presence of Protonix suggest that taking PPIs could cause a disturbance in the normal balance of flora found in the oral cavity and gastrointestinal tract, possibly leading to the long-term complications seen in some patients.

title: Confounding Logic: Peronist Disapproval and Support of Carlos Menem in Argentina
abstract: Argentine President Carlos Menem’s domination of the Peronist Party was a surprise to many. Menem’s implementation of free-market, neoliberal policies took the traditionally populist, union-based Peronist Party on an unprecedented rightward turn. Menem’s presidency was also marred by corruption scandals. Despite these developments and his deviation from the party line, however, Menem maintained the support of his party and was reelected. My thesis explains this phenomenon. Menem was successful for many reasons. His free-market reforms attracted the pro-business sector and the upper class, formerly anti-Peronist groups of voters. Menem’s economic reforms slashed Argentina’s soaring inflation rate and began to stabilize the economy, saving many from bankruptcy. The President forged strong alliances with party leaders from the provinces of Argentina, ensuring them their autonomy in exchange for their constituents’ support. Finally, he was also able to divide his opponents, keeping them from forming a successful coalition against him. Menem’s ultimate success, though, was premised on the weakly institutionalized nature of the Peronist Party. Menem’s ability to get away with corruption, the defeat of his opponents, his appeals to the upper-class and his alliance with provincial leaders were only possible in a party that lacked rigidity, clear rules and obvious channels for power. Peronist leaders were willing to overlook Menem’s corruption and anti-Peronist principals if their job-security, party funding and autonomy were assured. These leaders ensured the support of their constituents and Carlos Menem, an allegedly corrupt and in many ways anti-Peronista leader, was able to maintain his power for two terms.

title: Production of Carbon Nanotube Films as Conductive Substrates for Cardiomyocyte Growth
abstract: The research examined the production of optically transparent conductive substrates for in vitro studies of cardiac muscle cells. These muscle cells, cardiomyocytes, cause the heart to beat. Cardiomyocytes, when grown in vitro, lack intercellular electrical conduction, which leads to an asynchronous beating of heart cells. For future prospects of the implantation of these heart cells into the body, a biocompatible conductive substrate must be designed, which will enhance this cell communication. Carbon nanotube (NT) films are used for this purpose because of its intrinsic electrical conduction properties and apparent biocompatibility. Two methods, namely filtration and spin coating were used to produce these films. The filtration method is a reproducible means of creating uniform NT films, however the transfer of these films to transparent substrates for the observation of the heart cells was found to be tedious and difficult. A more direct way of creating the NT films on transparent substrates, spin coating was investigated, and methods of increasing throughput by parallel film production were designed. After production, the NT films were biofunctionalized using peptide amphiphiles (PA) in order to improve the biocompatibility with the cardiomyocytes. The films were surface characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), water contact angle measurements, and surface profilometry to investigate uniformity, biofunctionalization and thickness respectively.

title: Calumet Cluster Project Proposal
abstract: Natural resource damage has occurred in Indian Ridge Marsh (IRM), one of several marshlands adjacent to the Calumet Cluster Superfund site and a plan is needed for remediation and restoration IRM. The Calumet Cluster is a highly contaminated property on the South side of Chicago. Both hazardous and non-hazardous wastes were dumped, incinerated or stored here. Nothing on site prevents contaminated material from being transported by wind, surface, or groundwater to adjacent marshlands. Remediation activities for the site have been divided into three phrases: capping, groundwater control, and remediation. We are concerned with Phase III, which will assess and remediate areas surrounding the Cluster by claiming Natural Resource Damages under the Superfund Law. The party responsible for executing the remediation plans, as directed by the Superfund Law, is the Board of Trustees. The Board of Trustees is selected from government agencies such as US EPA, Illinois EPA, US Fish and Wildlife, among others. We will provide a priority list and remediation recommendations to the Board of Trustees to help guide the creation of the Natural Resource Damages Assessment (NRDA) and Restoration Plan for IRM. We will identify contaminants present and what can be done to remediate the marsh to “baseline conditions”. Once the site has been characterized, we hope to create a link between the contamination and the Cluster site, in order to identify the responsibilities of the Potentially Responsible Parties. We then will present our findings to the Board of Trustees, who will make the final decision for remediation plans for the site.

title: Light-weight Mirrors for Space-based Optics
abstract: Our project deals with the development of lightweight optical mirrors for use in space. The main idea is to develop a way to manufacture metallic mirrors that are both lighter and tougher for space purposes by combining the metal surfaces with composite backings that make them significantly lighter and stronger. These lighter mirrors are much easier and cheaper to launch into space. We have developed three main methods that can be used to create these mirrors. All three methods begin with a composite substrate in the shape of a 2-inch diameter puck produced by the Cornerstone Research Group (CRG). In the first method, the puck supplied by CRG also came with a thin layer of gold applied by CRG. We electroplated a layer of nickel (approximately 100 microns thick) onto the gold surface of the puck. The gold was needed to conduct the electricity needed to electroplate the nickel onto the surface, as the composite does not conduct sufficiently itself. The nickel layer was then polished to produce the mirrored surface. The second method takes a different approach by first vacuum depositing a layer of gold onto a piece of glass. The composite puck is then glued to the gold layer using an epoxy, and then the puck and gold removed because the gold does not adhere well to the glass. The puck is then electroplated with nickel and the nickel layer polished. The third method uses a different composite substrate provided by CRG that is electrically conductive enough to be directly electroplated onto. In this method, the nickel is directly electroplated onto the surface of the composite and then polished.

title: High and Mighty: A Cross-Cultural Look at the Phenomenon of Sanctioned Drug and Alcohol Use in War
abstract: There is a long and largely unacknowledged history of warriors and soldiers using drugs during battle, dating back to at least 2500 B.C.E. Substances ranging from natural opium and psychoactive mushrooms to rum and synthetic amphetamines have been utilized by cultures all over the world in wartime to improve performance by minimizing fear, increasing ferocity, and alleviating fatigue. Among the beneficiaries of this practice were the Berserk Vikings, the Incans, and the Zulu in their victories over the British. As a result of significant pharmacological advancements, however, the past hundred years have seen a significant increase in the use of drugs in war. Nearly every major combatant in World War II, including for Nazi Germany and the United States, distributed a combined total of amphetamine tablets in excess of 300 million to their pilots and soldiers. For the United States, use continues to have a significant role in military operations. This research highlights the pervasiveness of these practices and, by doing so, expands current frameworks of understanding both modern military pharmacology and war in general. The use of drugs and alcohol throughout history has proven beneficial to the physical effectiveness and mental survival of soldiers. Substances have managed the stresses and demands of war that have otherwise considerably limited individual performance. Despite the social stigma attached to drug use today, sanctioned drug and alcohol use in warfare remains an important tool in the 21st century.

title: Characterization of Seismicity in Alaska/Aleutian Subduction Zone
abstract: At subduction zones, the seismicity of the main thrust is clearly influenced by lateral heterogeneities such as asperities. By contrast, intermediate-depth seismicity is less well characterized and understood. Most studies have focused on across-slab seismicity variations such as double seismic zones. In this project, we identify clusters of intermediate depth seismicity in the Alaska/Aleutian subduction zones to reveal along-strike heterogeneities in the slab that may improve our understanding of stress sources and slab mechanics. We employed several cluster analysis techniques, the most successful being the Gath-Geva algorithm (GG), a fuzzy clustering technique, and the Gaussian mixture model (GMM). The two clearest clusters are identified by both methods. They are located near the Eastern end of Alaska subduction zone. The easternmost cluster corresponds to the segment C of Ratchkovski and Hansen (2002). This suggests that the cluster may be related to a material heterogeneity in the subducting plate or increased stress due to the differential motion of the neighboring slab segments. Three additional clusters may appear related to a possible tear in the subducting plate around longitude 180° possibly due to collision with the Bowers ridge. The anomalous focal mechanism of the 1906 Aleutian earthquake that occurred in that area is an additional evidence for this possible tear.

title: “W” Is For Working Class: How the Perception-Based Campaigns of George W. Bush Courted the White Working Class in 2000 and 2004
abstract: With George W. Bush as its candidate, the Republican Party’s success among white working class voters was significantly greater in the 2000 and 2004 presidential elections than in the elections of 1992 and 1996. What accounts for this substantial defection? Defining “working class” as earning less than median income—based on responses to each election year’s American National Election Study survey—and having no more than a high school education, this project aims to explore the ways in which perception became everything to the Bush campaigns. Though the white working class (WMC) is no longer strongly affected by campaign appeals along economic class lines, I argue that WMC members are still motivated to vote along cultural class lines by their perception of campaign values in close elections. To this end, this project explores the effects of rhetoric, framing, trust building, priming and message consistency in the Bush campaigns. Spring boarding off previous studies, I maintain that, even though the white working class may not agree with all the issue platforms of the Republican Party, national data shows that Bush was still successful in painting himself as a “preferred” candidate through the values and style of his campaigns. Issue positions alone, then, played a muted role in determining voting behavior in 2000 and 2004. Studying the ways in which campaign rhetoric and image framing affects the white working class demographic over these four election years is important because, in close elections, this is a swing demographic that, according to some, accounted for a majority of Bush’s victory margins in 2000 and 2004.

title: The Phenotypic Analysis of the Sleep/Wake Cycle in Neonatal Inbred Mouse Strains
abstract: The relationship between poor sleep and poor health underscores the need to identify the components of sleep that are genetically encoded. Studies in adult mice have revealed several sleep traits that are quantitatively driven by chromosomal elements. In the current study, we used a novel protocol to analyze sleep and wakefulness in pups from five inbred mouse strains. Pregnant females (14 days post-pregnancy) from each strain were housed in 14L:10D for the remainder of their gestational period. Food and water were available ad libitum. Newborn pups remained with their respective dams for nine days after delivery (approximately 18-21 days post-pregnancy). On postnatal day 9, pups were implanted with electromyographic (EMG) electrodes and were allowed to acclimate to the recording apparatus for 30 min after which sleep-wake patterns were continuously recorded for 120 min. The EMG waveforms were collected and manually scored. One-way ANOVA revealed that total amounts of wakefulness, active sleep (AS), and quiet sleep (QS) during the recording period, as well as the mean bout duration of each vigilant state were different between the strains. These data suggest that sleep-wake architecture in pups is under a significant degree of genetic regulation. Neonatal sleep-wake patterns are relatively independent of a) circadian regulation and b) the daily homeostatic challenges that govern sleep-wake architecture. In this respect, they represent sleep-wake regulation in its most fundamental state. In addition, AS and QS are considered precursors to REM and NREM sleep, respectively. Therefore, these results may be predictive of sleep regulation in adults.

title: Iron Abundance in Galaxy Clusters: Radial Dependence
abstract: Galaxy Clusters, large collections of galaxies gravitationally bound, are some of the most dynamic objects in the universe, where thousands of galaxies travel around at speeds as high as 1000 km/sec, all within an intracluster gas heated to as high as 100 million Kelvin. Galaxy clusters also seem to be very high in dark matter, as calculations determining the mass of these objects puts their expected masses at about 6 times what we can observe. Still unclear about these clusters is how they reached their high temperatures. By considering iron abundance as a function of position from the center of the cluster, I provide some evidence that, on average, the iron resides either closer to the core or closer to the outer components of the cluster. This data can also be used to calculate, again on average, the location of supernovae that are likely the source of energy required to heat this gas. Insights into these questions allow astronomers to gain insights into the formation of such enormous and dynamic systems.

title: Generation and Microbial Composition of Aerobic Granular Sludge
abstract: Compared to activated suspended sludge, treating wastewater with aerobic granular biomass results in superior liquid-biomass separation, high mixed liquor suspended solid (MLSS) concentrations, and the ability to meet high loading rates in biological wastewater treatment. In our study, operational parameters of a sequencing batch reactor were successfully modified to produce well-formed aerobic granules (1-3mm in diameter) performing efficient carbon and ammonia removal. Confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM) revealed that granules are composed of compactly organized biomass, which gives the granules a smooth appearance, with occasional “tufts” of filamentous microorganisms extending from the surface of the granules. To understand the mechanisms of granulation, it is important to obtain knowledge about the composition and structure of microbial communities residing in granules. We hypothesize that granular biomass harbors a different microbial community than flocular biomass. Our research aims at comparing microbial diversity and spatial relationships of microbial communities in aerobic granules and activated suspended sludge, which is used as the inoculum for granule formation. Studies utilizing the polymerase chain reaction (PCR) followed by denaturing gradient gel electrophoresis (DGGE), and fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH) coupled with CLSM are in progress. The data generated will deliver information about microbial diversity and spatial relationships in these specialized microbial communities.

title: Reading Their Lives. Oprah’s Book Club: Providing Women with Therapy, Community and Maternal Support
abstract: Despite the fact that the National Endowment for the Arts recently published a study that documented the current crisis of our literary culture, recording a loss of over 20 million readers in the past ten years, Oprah Winfrey has convinced unprecedented numbers of women to purchase and read novels through her Book Club. When Oprah airs a Book Club segment on The Oprah Winfrey Show, over five hundred thousand viewers have already read at least part of the book, and nearly as many buy the novel in the ensuing weeks. Oprah has been personally responsible for at least fifty of the best-selling novels in the past ten years, and she has been crowned the “most important person in books and media” by Newsweek magazine. This study seeks to illuminate how and why Oprah has inspired women to read in an era marked by literary apathy. Relying on the analysis of sociologist Pierrre Bourdieu, cultural critics Janice Radway, Nancy Chodorow, and Mimi White, as well as Oprah expert Eva Illouz, and Black feminist theorist Patricia Hill Collins, the project examines the precise nature of the reading practice promoted by Oprah and adopted by her viewers. Analyzing Oprah’s Book Club from a feminist prospective, I describe how Oprah has promoted a reading practice that—because it is based on superficial, not imaginative identification between reader and fictional character—is televisual rather than literary. Furthermore, Oprah mobilizes this female reading practice to promote the therapeutic mission of her show. Ultimately, this project suggests that Oprah has been able to popularize reading because of the therapeutic benefit her Book Club offers readers; figuring books as therapeutic tools, and using her Book Club to offer women a sense of maternal support, community and empowerment, Oprah and her Book Club offer women much more than the opportunity to read and discuss literature.

title: Predicting Congressional Elections: Regression Models
abstract: During every election season, potential candidates, political parties, journalists, and voters try to predict a given candidate’s likelihood of success. This paper, using data from the Federal Election Commission on congressional elections between 1992 and 2004, estimates a maximum-likelihood model to predict that probability. The probit regression model estimated uses only three factors: political party (relative to that of the current President), incumbency, and amount of contributions received (relative to those of other candidates in the same race). Though the FEC dataset contains many potential factors, none have as large an effect on a candidate’s probability of success as these three. Further, there are many benefits to this simple model. Most significantly, this model can predict with 95% accuracy the success of a given candidate for congress. Also, because the amount of contributions received is the only factor that is not known ex-ante, candidates can use the model as a tool to set fundraising goals. No other author has estimated a model to estimate an individual congressional candidate’s probability of success; indeed, few of the published papers on congressional elections even evaluate individual races. Most focus instead on predicting the change in the composition of congress – for example, how many seats the president’s party will lose. Though many papers predict presidential elections, their methods and models do not apply to congressional races. This paper, by contrast, provides a simple, accurate model for predicting the success of a congressional candidate.

title: Can Words Predict the Change in Future US Economic Growth?
abstract: What has happened to the ideological movement of US political parties over the past half-century? Does this movement have a relationship with “real life” variables such as GDP Growth? This project examines political party movement in a unique manner, using statistical textual analyses of political party platforms produced by the Democratic and Republican Parties from 1952-2004. A software program called Wordscore was invoked to produce a score for each document, placing each platform on a unidimensional continuum of economic policy. Results have shown that both parties have tended their economic agendas towards the left since the postwar period. More interestingly is the study of the divergence of the political parties from one another at critical times in our nation’s history. Why do the two parties converge in 1980 right before Reagan’s first term when the nation was experiencing terrible economic times? The time series data of political rhetoric divergence was compared to a time series data set of GDP growth, and a striking correlation was discovered. The finding suggests that the rhetoric used in creating party platform texts may actually be able to predict the change in the strength of the US economy. This project describes the methodology of the study in detail, also supposing theoretical hypotheses for this phenomenon.

title: Nacos and Fresas: Cultural Taste and Boundary-Making in Aguascalientes, Mexico
abstract: The study explores cultural tastes and boundary-making among emerging adults in Aguascalientes, Mexico. I focus on the cultural tastes of nacos and fresas—two social categories commonly used to label others. Although these terms lack a set definition, taste plays a crucial role in the categorization of individuals. Nacos tend to be vulgar and have bad taste, while fresas are inclined to be superficial and have cosmopolitan tastes. Over the past years, fresas have begun to appropriate naco tastes. I explore the reasons why fresas appropriate naco tastes and to what extent they embrace naconess. To understand this dynamic, I draw from cultural taste theories (Bourdieu 1984; Peterson 1992; Lamont 1992, 2000), which explain how taste is used as a mechanism to mark distinctions and how the tastes of the elite change. Over the summer of 2005, I conducted interviews and participant observation in Aguascalientes, Mexico. I selected an antro, or a club as the research site because antros reflect the ongoing changes and contradictions in the naco-fresa relationship. To complement the qualitative data, I employed an online survey on antro-going habits as they indicate cultural tastes. The data shows that, although fresas appropriate naconess, they do so in a selective manner. Fresas appropriate the positive aspects of naconess (i.e., music and carefree attitude) and reject negative attributes (i.e., vulgarity and ignorance). By appropriating naconess in a selective manner, fresas reinforce the boundaries between themselves and nacos. Antros maintain these boundaries through their selective admissions and by marking antros as places for fresas. The selective appropriation of naconess allows fresas to enlarge their cultural “toolkit” and to maintain their social privilege.

title: Synthesis South of the Border: Traditional Medicine and Biomedicine within the Mexican Public Health System
abstract: Biomedicine as a prominent healthcare paradigm often overshadows and threatens traditional healing and traditional medicine. Particularly, Mexico has a rich history and culture that include the use of traditional medicine and an excessive knowledge of alternative medicinal techniques. Thus, to examine the relationship between the public health sector and traditional healing in Mexico, numerous topics were assessed, including the extent to which traditional healing is currently practiced in Mexico and the locus and means of transmission of this medical knowledge. Next, the provision of adequate services within both the public and private sectors of Mexico were assessed through personal interviews coupled with questionnaires and participant observation. Roughly 86% of the Mexican population interviewed used some form of traditional medicine, including either medicinal plants or the services of traditional therapists. Research highlighted that the overall demand for traditional medicine in Mexico is not being met despite hopeful initiatives such as the development of integrated hospitals offering both traditional and allopathic medical services. The private sector is absorbing some of this responsibility through the creation of independent traditional healing centers that can provide both services and education to clients. However, the public health sector needs to recognize the vital role that traditional healing plays in the country of Mexico. More governmentally funded public efforts are needed to maintain the traditions of healing in Mexico and to treat medically this population while simultaneously respecting its cultural conceptions of disease and healing.

title: CO2 reduction to Methane/Methanol using Mixed Phase TiO2 Photocatalysts
abstract: The fundamental idea behind catalysis is to develop a material that will allow for the more efficient execution of a reaction. Photocatalysts use UV radiation and visible light to fuel reactions. Although there are many different forms of catalysts, the ones studied here are mixed phase titanium dioxide catalysts on a solid substrate. Previous research has shown there to be highly active catalytic sites at interfaces and defect sites in mixed phase TiO2 catalysts. Further exploration of this theory with specifically designed catalysts includes the synthesis of mixed-phase materials with solid-solid interfaces by a variety of techniques (sol-gel, physical vapor deposition, etc.). In order to compare the performance of these catalysts, a testing apparatus and protocol have been devised to evaluate each catalyst's ability to reduce gaseous CO2 to a mixture of methane and methanol. Investigation will also encompass the effects of pretreatment on surface morphology. Thermal oxidations and thermal reductions will be incorporated to clean the surface of the catalyst and activate surface sites, respectively. The ultimate goal of pretreatment is to increase photoactivity. Various microscopy methods will be employed to investigate any changes in surface morphology. In this presentation the reactor and experimental design will be presented as well as preliminary experimental results indicating system efficacy.

title: The Plight of Guernica: The Place of Picasso’s Masterpiece in the Spanish Memory
abstract: On April 26, 1937, during the Spanish Civil War, German and Italian forces bombed Guernica, Spain, which was not a military target. The reasons for the attack seem insufficient; Germany was officially doing this for Franco, but the horrific event was actually practice for the war brewing in Europe. Spanish artist Pablo Picasso chose the massacre as the subject of the mural he was commissioned to create by the Spanish Republican Government for the 1937 World’s Fair Exhibition in Paris. The resulting image, Guernica, has become one of Picasso’s most famous works. Scholars have debated this mural’s meaning to no avail, but it has come to immortalize the plight of the Spanish Republic and the return of democracy to Spain. My research explores the success of this image, both in commemorating the Spanish Civil War and in serving as a reminder of the horror and futility of warfare. The reason the image was successful results from the parallel experience of the painting and the Spanish people who survived the War. Picasso stipulated that the painting not be returned to Spain until democracy was restored, forcing the painting to find a new home until 1978. The situation was the same for many of the Spanish people; as long as Franco was in power, they had no home. Lastly, the project examines how the Spanish remembered Guernica through Picasso’s image, and the place of that memory in defining their own culture.

title: The Role of Stress in the Perception of Foreign Accents: Evidence From English-Accented French and French-Accented English
abstract: What is it about foreign accents that make them sound foreign? My study looks at English-accented French and French-accented English to find part of the answer to this question. One aspect of French that seems to be especially difficult for American English speakers to master is the pronunciation of unstressed vowels. In English, unstressed syllables are greatly reduced, meaning they are shorter in duration and less fully articulated; this is generally not the case in French. It has been shown that Japanese learners of English struggle to learn the correct rhythmic structure of English, and that this contributes to their perceived accent in English (Mochizuki-Sudo & Kiritani, 1991). Other studies have shown that native French speakers are typically stress “deaf,” that is, they have trouble perceiving stress contrasts (Peperkamp & Dupoux, 2002). In addition, the importance of segments must not be discounted, since individual vowels and consonants vary from one language to another. This research examines how important stress really is in the perception of foreign accents in French and in English. Results show that learners of French and of English do impose their native-language stress rules onto their target language. The finding suggests that prosodic structure is a particularly difficult aspect of second-language acquisition. It seems, however, that the degree to which a speaker imposes his or her native-language rules does not correlate with his or her perceived foreign accent. Furthermore, speakers’ accents were often rated differently if they were heard uttering a full sentence instead of one single word, suggesting there is some information necessary for judging accents that is not present in an individual word. Thus, in foreign accents, stress matters some; but segmentals seem to matter a lot.

title: A Novel Synthesis of Oxazolidines via the Catalytic [3 + 2] Coupling of Aziridines and Organic Carbonyls
abstract: An outstanding challenge in organic and medicinal chemistry is the rapid and efficient generation of nitrogen-containing heterocycles such as oxazolidines, 5-membered cyclic rings with two heteroatoms, nitrogen and oxygen, flanking a carbonyl group. These compounds have been shown to be present in many biologically active natural products and can be used as pro-drugs in drug delivery applications. Their biological activity is derived from a structure that straddles two biologically important structural motifs: β-amino alcohol and β-amino acid. Their ability to function as pro-drug is facilitated by masking the β-amino alcohol functionality within the ring, which also allows for increased lipophilicity and ease of entry through the lipid bi-layer in cells. As such, oxazolidines are very attractive targets in synthesis. Traditionally, oxazolidines have been synthesized through the coupling of a β-amino alcohol to either diethylcarbonate or phosgene. Such procedures are often atom-uneconomic and inefficient, in addition to being hazardous (as in the case of phosgene). In contrast, the [3+2] catalytic coupling of aziridines and organic carbonyls could provide a safe and highly efficient alternative to oxazolidines in one step. The high reactivity of the aziridine ring would allow it to undergo an efficient coupling with carbonyl electrophiles in a one-pot reaction under mild reaction conditions. In addition, the ready availability of a variety of aziridines and carbonyl substrates will allow for facile extension of this coupling methodology into a diverse range of oxazolidines. We have demonstrated that a variety of aldehydes can readily be coupled to aziridines, yielding 4 and 5 substituted oxazoldines in the presence of a scandium triflate catalyst. We have also extended this [3+2] coupling to a wide range of ketones.

title: Air Pollution in Poland: The Effects of European Union Integration on Environmental Governance
abstract: In May 2004, Poland became a member of the European Union (EU) and now its obligation to comply with environmental laws is more pressing. Poland will need to show that it can stand alone as an environmental citizen of the EU. This project focuses on air pollution policy in Poland as an example of how environmental governance functions there. With a focus on sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, and particulate matter, the research has found that (a) the nature of air pollution, including source and location, has remained largely the same in Poland over the past 10 years, except for a shift from stationary to mobile sources of nitrogen oxides; (b) Poland has significantly changed the content of its air pollution regulations to harmonize them with EU Directive, yet it has retained some of its most effective environmental policy tools; and (c) that the most significant challenges remaining for Poland as an environmental citizen of the EU concern funding and citizen involvement. My study utilizes the most recent air pollution data and attempts to paint a picture of Poland’s air using maps and is based on a visit to Poland in the summer of 2005, when I met with environmental personnel, collected data, and familiarized myself with Poland’s geography. This project was implicitly informed by a comparison to U.S. environmental policy, allowing for several unique insights.

title: The Effect of Perceptual Versus Conceptual Pronoun Phrases on Self-Awareness During Vigilance Tasks: An Investigation of Attention as a Function of Spatiotemporal Focusing
abstract: Individuals differ considerably from one another in their abilities to focus attention on environmental stimuli. Specifically, human attention is of limited capacity and there are two broad sources competing for the spotlight of our attention at any given moment. Conceptual information, such as knowledge of the current month, generally involves constructs derived from specific instances or occurrences that already exist in the mind as a product of mental activity. Perceptual information, on the other hand, tends to center around recognition and interpretation of sensory stimuli, which requires some consciousness of the surrounding environment. The phenomenon of spatiotemporal focusing, with respect to self-awareness, is a new theoretical construct that simply describes how tightly or diffusely one’s attention is localized to the present time and place. The present study was designed to build on previous research investigating self-awareness and attention, and to introduce spatiotemporal focusing as a relevant variable for predicting behavior. In particular, we sought to define “attentional focus” in terms of blinking frequency and skin conductance level, in order to validate the idea that self-awareness is accompanied by attentional changes, or spatiotemporal focus. Based on prior knowledge of Duval and Wickland’s Objective Self-Awareness theory, we developed a novel, self-awareness test in which participants were presented with a mixture of various pronoun phrases. The effect of variables such as type of pronoun (self versus other) and type of phrase (perceptual versus conceptual) were then examined in relation to self-awareness and spatiotemporal focusing.

title: The Impact of Stress on Personality and Negative Cognitive Style
abstract: This study examined whether life stress variables predicted changes in any of an individual’s Big 5 personality traits or negative cognitive style (Abramson, Metalsky, & Alloy, 1989). The study used data from a one-year follow-up of the first cohort of adolescents (N =211) participating in a larger longitudinal study examining risk factors for depression and anxiety disorders. At two time points, approximately 14 months apart, participants underwent a semi-structured life stress interview assessing episodic and chronic life stress over the previous year, and completed a battery of self-report questionnaires assessing the Big 5 personality traits and negative cognitive style. Cross-sectional correlations at both time points revealed significant positive relationships between chronic stress and both neuroticism and negative cognitive style, and significant negative relationships between chronic stress and extraversion, conscientiousness, and agreeableness. Results from hierarchical linear regression models indicated that chronic stress, especially interpersonal chronic stress, significantly predicted levels of neuroticism and extraversion at Time 2 beyond the effects of the Time1 levels of those personality traits. No significant correlations were found between episodic stress and the outcome measures. It has been known for some time that individuals who are high on neuroticism tend to generate some of the stress in their lives, but this study is the first to demonstrate that chronic stress may also predict personality factors beyond their general levels of stability. Therefore, these factors will need to be taken into consideration in developing complex models of the etiology of mood and anxiety disorders.

title: Spaces of Resistance, Moments of Freedom: Hip-Hop on the Margins of Guayaquil, Ecuador
abstract: Invisibilidad, oscuridad, peligro Viviendo en los márgenes Viviendo una vida invisible Tú, tus calles, tus cuentos En búsqueda de una voz Pero que gana una voz sin audiencia (es realmente una voz?...una voz silenciosa tiene algun valor?) Sean la audiencia ¡Atención! les presento la cultura hip-hop Guayaquil Guayaquil is Ecuador's largest city with a population of approximately three million people, most of whom live in poverty and rarely occupy the attention of those who promote Guayaquil as a rich tourist attraction and as one of the world's emerging cities. As politicians and city leaders invest more and more resources to reconstruct downtown Guayaquil and other strategic locales (luxurious malls, riverwalks, five-star hotels), the majority of the city's residents sink deeper into despair due to increasing unemployment, frequent outbreaks of disease, decaying schools, a lack of drinking water, and violence. It is within this context that the phenomenon of hip-hop has emerged in Guayaquil. Marginalized youth and adults have taken this genre that has been commercialized around the globe and have adopted it to express their specific life experiences and views of society. Hip-hop originated in New York City in the 1970s and includes rap, break dance, and graffiti. During the last fifteen years, immigration and the Internet have exposed Guayaquil to these forms of expression. My study explores how Guayaquil's urban poor use these means of expression to describe their experiences as members of a city that discriminates and stereotypes them to such extremes that they are not allowed to serve as vital community members who have skills and ideas that can contribute to the progress of their society. Through an exploration of sight and space, I analyze hip-hoppers' quest for visibility and respect.

title: Investigation of Virus-cell Fusion: Activation and Inactivation of Paramyxovirus Fusion Proteins
abstract: The Paramyxoviridae family consists of enveloped, negative-stranded RNA viruses that cause significant disease in both animals and humans. Simian virus 5 (SV5), human parainfluenza virus 3 (hPIV3), and Newcastle disease virus (NDV), members of Paramyxoviridae, have been studied extensively as a model for cellular entry and fusion for the paramyxovirus family and class I viruses as a whole. Fusion of these viruses with cells requires the action of two glycoproteins; hemaglutinin-neuraminidase (HN) serves as a receptor-binding protein that triggers fusion mediated by the fusion protein (F). Mutations within the F protein can alter its HN dependence, fusion activity, and reaction kinetics. To further explore the effects of these mutations, the temperature dependence and temperature of inactivation for SV5 mutants were examined. Mutants were evaluated using two fusion assays: a syncytium formation assay and fluorescent dye transfer assay. In addition, previously identified mutations that affect fusion mediated by the F proteins of SV5 and NDV are being introduced into the hPIV3 F protein. The crystal structure of hPIV3 F protein was recently solved, raising questions regarding its regulation and conformational changes related to cellular fusion. Analysis of the effect of these mutations on hPIV3 fusion in the context of a known protein structure may clarify the mechanisms of fusion and may elucidate mechanisms of viral entry.

title: Parental Couple Conflict as a Predictor of Child Temperament Traits
abstract: This project examines how children’s temperament traits are related to interactions between their parents. More specifically, it asks if there is a link between how parents resolve conflict in the marital relationship and child temperament traits. To test this question, child participants between the ages of 3 and 6 completed ten tasks designed to measure individual differences in temperament traits while being videotaped from behind a two-way mirror. In a separate visit, parents completed standardized discussion tasks measuring couple interaction conflict and conflict resolution while also being videotaped. This observational data was supplemented by self-report questionnaires measuring the marital relationship. Understanding predictors of child temperament traits is important because evidence suggests that a child’s temperament may be an important risk factor for the emergence of psychopathology, particularly depression (Caspi, Moffitt, Newman, & Silva, 1996). Furthermore, previous research findings indicate that discordant family environments have negative effects on children, including higher levels of externalizing and internalizing behavioral problems in young children (Grych & Fincham, 1990). Importantly, family studies of child risk have often neglected the role of fathers. This study is unique in that relationship behaviors of both mothers and fathers were assessed.

title: The Effects of Symbolic Play on Children’s Understanding of Letters
abstract: Starting at an early age, children are often exposed to a variety of letter and number toys. Parents stick magnetic letters and numbers on the refrigerator, float similar toys in the bathtub, and encourage their children to play with letter blocks and numbers. Likewise, preschool teachers use similar items in their classrooms, believing that these toys will help children learn the complex symbol systems of letters and numerals. The assumption that concrete objects are inherently beneficial in teaching young children is supported by the work of classic developmental theorists. However, more recent research has questioned this belief, suggesting that it is difficult for children to understand a symbolic object (such as a letter toy) both as an object in its own right and as a symbol for something else. It appears that only specific play that emphasizes the symbolic properties of letters or numbers may promote symbolic understanding. For example, using letter magnets to represent words may facilitate understanding of the relation between spoken and written language. To test the hypothesis that specific forms of play with concrete symbolic objects will promote children’s symbolic understanding, we have designed a set of activities that use letter toys as symbolic representations. Initial results suggest that guided interaction with these objects may be very helpful in children’s acquisition of symbolic understanding of letters, whereas undirected interaction may actually be counterproductive. These results, which encourage specific and guided play with symbolic objects, may eventually bring practical knowledge to early education curricula.

title: Evaluating Diabetes Treatment Methods in Urban Morocco
abstract: Developing countries are experiencing an epidemiological transition in which noncommunicable diseases like type II diabetes are replacing communicable diseases as major causes of mortality. Such is the case in Morocco, specifically in urban areas where over 11% of the population has type II diabetes. Fortunately, there are proven methods of diabetes treatment and prevention. Diabetes treatment in the US generally is based on the following health model of sequential steps: 1) physician provision of medical information 2) patient understanding 3) patient self-care behaviors and 4) improved clinical results. Yet many patients find it difficult to perform these self-care behaviors and make the appropriate lifestyle changes that lead to improved clinical results. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the health model most commonly used in diabetes treatment in urban Morocco. It was found that physicians in Morocco attempted to follow the same health model used in the US for diabetes treatment but were often unsuccessful in achieving improved clinical results. Five major factors contributed to the flaws of the model: 1) socioeconomic status, 2) cultural influences, 3) the physician’s role, 4) the gender-age-socioeconomic overlap, and 5) Morocco’s health care system. Based on the faults of the current health model, a new, improved health model is proposed that addresses these issues.

title: Production of Inflectional and Derivational Morphology: An fMRI Study
abstract: The study identifies and compares the neural mechanisms that underlie the production of two types of words—inflections and derivations—to determine if they are processed in similar or different regions of the brain. Derivations, words in which addition of a suffix changes the category of a word (grass = noun vs. grassy = adjective), are different from inflected words in which additions of suffixes do not change categories of words (doll = noun vs. dolls = noun). Traditionally, it is believed that inflections are processed in the anterior (front) of the brain, whereas derivation is processed more posteriorly. This belief is challenged by the Fix (2005) study in which individuals with Broca’s aphasia (individuals who have difficulty with language production because of anterior brain damage/disease) cannot produce pseudo-derived words. Why can individuals who have intact posterior brain regions not produce words thought to be processed in the front of the brain? To answer this question, an fMRI study was conducted to determine the site in the brain young, normal adults produce derived and inflected words. If the primary structures necessary for the production of these words is revealed, it will help demystify why individuals with Broca’s aphasia may or may not be able to produce these kinds of words. The experiment also allows a broader discussion of the content and site of inflected and derived morphology produced as per traditional linguistic models of word production.

title: Gopher Politics: Minnesota, Farmer-Laborism, and the Rise of the Democratic Party from 1915-1948
abstract: When most people think of the Democratic Party, images of the Democratic Donkey are on the forefront of our minds. First used as a symbol for Andrew Jackson’s “jackass” populist views, the Donkey continued to represent different factions of the Democratic Party throughout the 19th and 20th Century. While this symbol continues to signify the Democratic Party today, I argue that in the years of 1935-1968, the symbol of the Democratic Party should not be the Donkey, but a Minnesota Gopher instead. In analyzing the influences and forces leading to the rise of the Democratic Party during the years following the Democrats disaster at Madison Square Gardens in 1924, I maintain that the correct symbol for the revival of the Democratic Party should be the ferocious, yet lovable, Minnesota Gopher. The political history of the Gopher State, and especially the Minnesota Farmer-Labor Party of 1922 to 1944, provides historians with a better explanation of how the Democratic Party transformed from a party based primarily in the South to an urban-focused northern party. When Franklin D. Roosevelt enacted the now infamous New Deal reforms, he was not enacting a set of reforms that was necessarily new or innovated. Instead, the New Deal was the culmination of a long history of progressive movements and representative of new national party loyalties. And as the Democratic Party embarked upon a new era of Civil Rights legislation, these new party loyalties became vital to the continued success of Democratic reforms. In understanding these great shifts, no history can overlook the importance of the lovable, yet ferocious, Gopher State.

title: Spirochete: An Analysis of Gender, Venereal Disease, and Stigma
abstract: This paper studies Spirochete, a Living Newspaper about syphilis, produced by the Federal Theatre Project. The play premiered in Chicago in 1938 amidst a national campaign to combat venereal disease and Chicago’s program was one of the most successful. Despite the campaign, syphilis remained a stigmatized and controversial issue – a disease associated with illicit sexuality and low “others”. In the paper I argue that the play unintentionally perpetuates many of these stereotypes as a result of its uncritical use of conventional gender stereotypes. While the play does dispel some of the stigmas associated with syphilis, it does so exclusively for white middle-class men. In making syphilis safe for such men, Spirochete nonetheless classifies women and minorities as diseased threats to the social body. In contrast, the play portrays the medical profession in heroic terms, as capable, not only of curing syphilis, but also of replacing misdirected moralism with scientific truths. For the project, I conducted research in the Federal Theatre Project’s archives and consulted contemporary magazines and newspapers. I also engaged in close textual analysis and situated the play in its historical context. The existing body of research on the play is limited to short articles or a brief mention as part of larger works. My thesis adds to the existing body of literature by including a detailed textual analysis, necessary to understand the issues of stigma and gender.

title: Protected Values and the Evaluation of Moral Arguments
abstract: This study explores trends in evaluating moral arguments. While several psychology models explain the extent of reason and emotion in making moral judgments and the factors that constitute a moral infraction, there is little research on how moral judgments are perceived by those who have protected values. Individuals with protected values tend to not weigh the consequences of an action but focus on the action itself; studies have shown that in making decisions involving protected values, individuals choose actions that contradict the normative decisions determined by the consequentialist model. As judgment of moral arguments is a common and important activity, it would be of interest to determine what factors affect how moral arguments are perceived. Researchers developed a moral judgment questionnaire, which intended to study the effects of individual protected values, deontological versus consequential arguments, and multiplicity of reasons on moral judgment. Results indicate that while there is a main effect of multiplicity and type of argument, there is only a small, nonsignifcant effect of protected values. Further studies may find a significant effect of protected values.

title: Educational Experimentation: Nixon's Experimental Schools Program and Perry County, Mississippi
abstract: Educational Experimentation analyzes the school desegregation and innovative educational reform that restructured an impoverished rural area in Mississippi in the 1970’s. Two years after the county started desegregation of its schools in 1971, Perry County was one of 19 school districts to participate in the federal Experimental Schools (ES) Program. The ES program sought to use local control to implement district-wide reformation through 5 years of funding that doubled the Perry County district’s annual budget. Federal officials prevented the district from using the grant money to finance the basic operational costs that burdened the schools, however. The Perry County school district was incapable of pioneering innovative education when the community could not sustain a rudimentary system of education. This project is based upon three months of research of federal documents and policies, as well as local newspapers and school board minutes from 1970-1979, accessed through a visit to the Mississippi State Archives and the Perry County School District. Despite the fact that many remnants of the ES program continue to resurface in American education reform, the ES program has not been written about since the early 1980’s. While many of the details of this project are specific to Perry County, the findings and analysis of the process by which desegregation and education policy were implemented in this district relate to the experiences of impoverished districts across the country, rural and urban, both in the 1970’s and today as they continually negotiate local and federal control.

title: Theoretical Radial Velocity Distributions of Double Neutron Star Systems
abstract: The radial velocity component of binary pulsars, such as PSR J037-3039, is an important statistic in determining the properties and formation history of binary pulsar systems. However, the radial component of a binary pulsar’s velocity cannot be determined from observation. Although we cannot ascertain the radial velocity of double neutron stars (DNS) observationally, population synthesis calculations can provide us with reasonable guidance on the expected radial velocity distribution of DNS. By using the StarTrack population synthesis code in conjunction with the observed density function of massive binaries in the galaxy we were able to generate a theoretical population of DNS. By then evolving the motion of these systems in the galactic potential to the current era and calculating the radial velocity of the DNS relative to the sun, we are able to construct theoretical radial velocity distributions for double neutron star systems. We find that the derived radial velocity distributions are very well approximated by a Gaussian distribution centered at zero with standard deviations ranging from 60 to 200 km s-1. In addition, the standard deviation of the distribution is dependant on the parameters used in the nascent kick velocity imparted to the DNS system upon birth of the neutron stars. This analysis was part of a larger study conducted on the formation and progenitors of PSR J0373-3039. Our paper can be found on astro-ph at astro-ph/0602024.
