Finally, I will attempt to show how by removing the category distinction between literature and other forms of art, one can, with the help of Blanchot’s understanding of the future aesthetic object, the Book to come, resolve this problem of manifest difference in intersubjective communication through a conceptual union of the subject/object difference—the initial dialectical moment of discursive communication—as a post-discursive, pan-subjective understanding of mediated expression thought of in terms of the medium's inherent limitations.

title: The Optimization of a Blast Resistant Steel Alloy
abstract: On October 12, 2000 an attack on the USS Cole left seventeen American sailors dead. This vulnerability to attack started the development of blast resistant steel alloys. Several iterations of blast resistant steels have been developed; however, the materials have yet to meet the performance goals balance of high uniform ductility, yield strength above 120 ksi, optimized austenite stability, shear instability resistance, and fracture toughness above 90 ksi/in0.5. In the latest iteration of blast resistant alloys, known as TRIP-120, it was discovered that a discontinuous cellular reaction was forming at the grain boundaries, lowering uniform ductility. This cellular reaction was prevented through a novel two step heat treatment where the first temperature was designed to precipitate discrete γ’ particles at the grain boundaries effectively pinning them in place, followed by a regular tempering treatment to precipitate the rest of the γ’ necessary to meet the strength goal. While this was successful at preventing the discontinuous reaction from proceeding; SEM analysis of dynamic tension samples revealed a susceptibility to intergranular fracture. In addition the two-step tempering processing did not allow for effective tempering control of the austenite stability temperature. In an effort to solve these issues two plates of the material were warm rolled at 450C to twenty percent reduction and forty percent reduction respectively. Thermo-calc computation was used to predict the effect on the required tempering cycle necessary to meet the performance goals and experimental work was conducted to calibrate the models yielding an effective processing method.

title: Neuronal Toxicity of Amyloidogenic Peptides in C. elegans Models
abstract: In neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s disease, Huntington’s diseases, and the lesser known familial Danish dementia, specific proteins misfold and aggregate, usually resulting in the loss of natural function as well as a potential gain of proteotoxic function. The aggregation and accumulation of these proteins (Aβ in Alzheimer’s disease, expanded polyglutamine stretches in huntingtin in Huntington’s disease, and ADan in familial Danish dementia) eventually lead to cellular dysfunction and cell death. These aggregating proteins are expressed throughout the brain, but only specific parts of the brain are affected depending on the disease. In order to compare the proteotoxic effects of these different aggregating proteins on the neurons, I have generated a new C. elegans model with pan-neuronal expression of YFP::ADan, which I have compared to existing models expressing Aβ and polyglutamine. Several behavioral assays were used to examine the function of different subsets of neurons: a thrashing motility assay for motor neurons, pharyngeal pumping for the pharyngeal nervous system, and the chemotaxis response for chemosensory neurons. I have found that ADan affects different subsets of neurons than Aβ and polyglutamine, thus even in a C. elegans model system with only 302 neurons, aggregating proteins affect subsets of neurons differently.

title: The Ontological Argument for the Existence of God
abstract: First presented by Saint Anselm, and later solidified by Rene Descartes, the Ontological Argument for the Existence of God is one of the most ingenious philosophical arguments ever presented. The argument claims that we can prove the existence of God from the very idea of it. Just as we can determine from the idea of a triangle that it must have three sides, so too, we can determine from the idea of God (as perfect) that it must exist (as it would otherwise be imperfect). Echoing a historically representative sentiment, Bertrand Russell wrote of the argument that “it is easier to feel convinced that it must be fallacious than it is to find out precisely where the fallacy lies.” I try to demonstrate that the argument is sound, and that it deserves far more philosophical credence than it has traditionally received. Although many objections have been raised to the argument, I argue that they do not hold up to critical analysis, and that the responses to many of them are actually contained within the text of Descartes’ original argument, or otherwise in his published letters. A modern take on the argument by Norman Malcolm further helps make its strength apparent, and provides an excellent framework for responding to objections. While I identify several weakness and assumptions in the argument, I do not find them sufficiently damaging to warrant its widespread rejection. I thus conclude that despite being historically unpersuasive, the argument is nonetheless valid and true, and that therefore, God exists.

title: Sonographic Quantitative Sensory Testing of the Bladder
abstract: A shortcoming in the diagnosis of painful pelvic disorders is the inability to find reliable clinical correlations between the objective measure of bladder volume and the associated subjective measure of bladder sensitivity. Cystometry and catheterization have been established as the gold standard of investigating lower urinary tract symptoms for the last thirty years. However, due to catheterization, cystometric studies are uncomfortable for the patient, expose women to a risk of bladder infection, and may not accurately reflect bladder function in that they impose a retrograde stimulation onto the bladder’s afferent nerves. Consequently, there is a need for a safer, reliable, noninvasive and more naturalistic method of quantifying relative visceral sensitivity in order to assess bladder function. In this project, the objective was to assess the validity and reliability of an alternative, more naturalistic method for determining bladder sensory thresholds: three dimensional transabdominal sonographic measurement of bladder volumes. We performed two sets of three-dimensional ultrasound measures of bladder sensory threshold volumes in 49 healthy female volunteers. Sensory levels corresponding to cystometric first sensation, first urge, and maximum tolerance were quantified and related to self-reported visual analogue scores for bladder urgency and pain. Sonographic measurement of bladder sensory urgency volumes produced valid estimates resembling those determined with traditional invasive cystometry. The interrater reliability was high and the one-week retest reliability was superior to conventional cystometry. The robust diagnostic test characteristics and obvious noninvasive nature of sonographic cystometry suggest this approach has utility in both experimental and clinical assessment of multiple genitourinary disorders.

title: Development of Au-Ag Nanorods for Antibacterial Coatings on Biomedical Devices
abstract: With numerous infections being caused by surgical implantation of biomedical devices every year, there is a need to suppress and inhibit bacterial growth on the device’s surface. Applied directly to a surface, a coating has the ability to interact with the environment. I proposed a dual technology that can deter bacterial infections. The design criteria for an antibacterial coating on these surfaces include physiological stability, good biocompatibility, and the ability to prevent and suppress infection over a long period of time. My approach was to develop coatings for biomedical relevant substrates that contain plasmonic Au nanorods, silver ions and polydopamine. Because of their unique optical properties and low toxicity, Au nanorods were synthesized and created to have peak extinction at 787nm. We characterized the nanorods by UV-Vis-NIR spectroscopy and TEM. My research demonstrates that silver ions, having antibacterial properties, can be attached to Au nanorods using polydopamine as an adhesive. By taking advantage of its adhesive properties, I also used polydopamine to incorporate the Ag-Au nanorods to the TiO2 surface. This methodology has the potential to be used in the development of materials resistant to bacterial infections.

title: That Which I Know in Principle: Cultivating Development and Youth Nationalism in Oman's Education Sector
abstract: Since the 1970’s, the Sultanate of Oman has undergone continuous and significant changes in all areas of society. In just under 40 years, the current sultan, HM Sultan Qaboos bin Sai’d, has led the country in developing new roads, hospitals, businesses, municipal areas and educational institutions, and has initiated a policy of Omanisation to replace expatriate workers with Omani nationals. Oman has been characterized by self-isolation from tourism and international involvement, tribal politics, a multiplicity of ethnic identities existing under a single “Omani” national title, and a very young population. With numerous rapid developments and greater integration into the global community, significant changes in culture and national awareness were inevitable. Despite multiple definitions of culture and tradition that exist within the sultanate, the state has succeeded in defining a nationalist and patriotic drive amongst its citizens to continue future development as a national entity. This research examines how the Omani education system creates, encourages, and maintains a sense of nationalism and national culture within Oman’s student population. Through interviews with educational employees as well as interviews with and surveys of university students, this study examines how development and national philosophy are translated into youth culture and how the government has created a national mentality that has enabled a territory characterized by tribal solidarity and lack of infrastructure to grow into a united, modern and prosperous state in less than four decades.

title: Does Stakeholder Alignment Correlate with Higher Student Performance? Evidence from KIPP Schools
abstract: In the quest to replicate successful schools, analysis must go beyond test scores to understand what characteristics, traits, and trends are associated with higher achieving schools. The Knowledge is Power Program, known as the KIPP network, is widely regarded as the highest achieving charter school movement and a model of national education reform. In their Healthy Schools and Regions Initiative, KIPP recognizes that while student achievement results are important, they are not the only indicators that define school health; other domains including academic curriculum, college preparatory support, human capital, culture and climate, and school leadership contribute considerably to a healthy and high performing school. Furthermore, a healthy school community comprises multiple stakeholders including students, teachers, parents, staff, and principals. This study uses the data from the KIPP 2008-2009 pilot survey and seeks to identify the characteristics in the Healthy Schools survey data associated with strong test score performance. It quantifies the measure of agreement (referred to as alignment) between the five referenced stakeholders across the five domains and regresses it against national test score performance. Data examines domain-specific alignment and stakeholder-pair alignment at the end of year tests and also notes the change in test score performance during the academic year. Preliminary evidence suggests that certain elements of stakeholder alignment correlate with student test performance. While overall results are not available at this time, it is hoped they will contribute to a better understanding of what kind of school culture breeds success so that it may be replicated in education reform.

title: Nucleosome Positioning in the Malaria Parasite
abstract: DNA folds tightly around protein complexes called nucleosomes in order to fit inside our cells. DNA must bend sharply to coil around a nucleosome, and some sequences are more flexible than others. This means that nucleosomes prefer to wrap certain sequences. Previous work demonstrates that the yeast genome uses these preferences to encode favored locations for its nucleosomes. Although the “nucleosome positioning code” successfully explains much of the organization of nucleosomes in yeast, nucleosome positioning in higher eukaryotes is less precisely understood for many reasons. One reason is that mammalian genomes contain very large regions of A+T-rich DNA, and A+T-rich sequences are preferentially excluded from nucleosomes in yeast. This means that the sequence motifs that enable A+T rich sequences to wrap into nucleosomes are unknown. Plasmodium falciparum, the causative agent of malaria, has a highly A+T rich genome. Studying nucleosome organization in the P. falciparum genome will allow nucleosome positioning preferences in A+T rich DNA to be determined. This is an important step to be taken before nucleosomal organization is understood in higher eukaryotes. I have obtained ~10 million nucleosomal sequences from P. falciparum. Analysis of these sequences indicates that like yeast, much of the organization of nucleosomes is encoded by the genome. However, P. falciparum nucleosomal sequences appear to lack the characteristic sequence preferences that define nucleosome positions in all other eukaryotes studied. This suggests that there are novel nucleosome sequence preferences in A+T rich DNA, and I am now working to delineate these undiscovered motifs.

title: Living in Between: How Rural to Rural Migrants Navigate Transnational Lives
abstract: Previous literature on transnational migration has studied migrants moving to urban centers in the United States. This study looks at a population we’ve missed: those who travel to rural receiving regions. The major forces that previous researchers have argued maintain transnational contact are political, religious and social organizations that are all but nonexistent for the migrants arriving in rural regions. This study explores the nuances of transnational life when it is anchored in rural areas of both the sending and receiving countries. Findings are based on a qualitative study of five immigrant families living in rural Western New York and their relatives in San Juan Mixtepec, a small indigenous community in Oaxaca, Mexico. The nature of rural life means people are isolated. No hometown organization helps Mixtepec migrants maintain contact with each other or anyone back home, and Oaxacan politicians do not worry about reaching out to a Western New York contingent of citizens. Furthermore, there are few options for religious involvement in Spanish and no opportunities to worship in Mixteco. Yet these immigrants still live transnational lives, maintaining ties to their home and culture through personal agency, not institutional support. Findings in this study fill a hole in our knowledge of transnational migration by focusing on rural to rural migrants. A revision of theory is necessary with a focus on non-institutional maintenance of transnational ties to fully understand the lived experience of these migrants, a population that comprises almost the entirety of the foreign farmworker population.

title: Unraveling the Catalytic Mechanism of Topoisomerase V
abstract: Found in all three domains of life, topoisomerases are ubiquitous enzymes that relax supercoiled DNA. Their function is thus essential to solving the topological problems that result from replication, transcription, and recombination. While previously discovered topoisomerases fit into the current classification scheme, structural studies suggest that the recently isolated Topoisomerase V is the first member of a new class. In particular, the unusual arrangement of five putative active site residues within a unique fold implies that “TopoV” utilizes a novel catalytic mechanism of DNA cleavage and religation. Structural analyses and mutational studies have supported this proposal, but details of the mechanism remain unclear. Specifically, although TopoV likely utilizes a mechanism involving transesterification, we do not know which amino acids act as the general acid catalysts, general base catalysts, and transition state stabilizers. To assign these roles, I investigated the catalytic characteristics of the five putative active site residues: Arginine-131, Arginine-144, Histidine-200, Glutamic acid-215, and Lysine-218. I introduced conservative and non-conservative substitutions of these amino acids in either one or two fragments of TopoV. I then assayed the DNA relaxation activity of the mutants and compared the mutational effects to wild-type activity. My results showed that R131, H200, E215, and K218 are not the general acid or base catalysts. They also implicated R131, H200, and K218 in transition state stabilization and demonstrated the essentiality of R144. This study is the first step towards understanding the novel solution that TopoV uses to solve the universal problem of DNA relaxation.

title: Incorporating Regional Variances Into the Measure of Concentration for the United States Airline Industry
abstract: Measuring industry concentration is dependent on the definition of the relevant market. Without a proper market definition, measures of concentration may fail to capture the true market situation facing the consumer. In addition, in order to study the social effects of market concentration, the measures of concentration must be depicted accurately. The Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI) is the most common measure of industry concentration. For the domestic airline industry, an HHI with a market defined on the national level fails to capture the geographically imbalanced nature of the airline industry, with airlines possessing great market power at certain airport hubs and having almost no presence at many other airports. To remedy this shortcoming, I propose two types of modified HHI calculations, one with a market defined on the airport level and the other with a market defined on the airport pair (route) level. Improving upon the common method of measuring industry concentration will allow researchers to obtain a more correct picture of the airline industry, enabling them to better predict the social effects of changes in market concentration.

title: The Search for a Vaccine: An Investigation of Genes in Neisseria Species
abstract: Every year, there are approximately 800,000 cases of gonorrhea in the United States. Additionally, pelvic inflammatory disease, which is caused by gonorrhea, affects about one million women annually. If left untreated, this sexually transmitted disease can lead to infertility and severe complications related to pregnancy. Gonorrhea is caused by infections of the bacteria Neisseria gonorrhoeae in the genital tract, mouth and anus. Another bacterium of the Neisseria species, Neisseria meningitidis, is best known as the causititive agent of meningitis. 10% of the 2500-3000 annual cases of meningitis in the United States lead to death. The mechanisms of these Neisseria species were the topic of my research for the past four summers. The HFQ gene synthesizes an abundant RNA binding protein in many bacteria, and my goal was to further define its role in N. gonorrhoeae by engineering a strain of N. gonorrhoeae that lacks this gene. Growth experiments with this mutant strain would help to better define the HFQ gene and the genes that control it in N. gonorrhoeae. My research also aimed to investigate iron regulated genes (sdh, tonB, sodB and fur) in both species. Iron homeostasis is a key metabolism in both N. gonorrhoeae and N. meningitidis, and increased data about these iron regulated genes might point to vaccine candidate gene.

title: Public School Compliance with Special Education Laws in the State of Illinois: A Case Study of Evanston/Skokie School District 65, and How Parents, As Non-Legal Actors, Force the District to Comply with the Laws
abstract: Special education has truly progressed over the past few years. Before the 1970s, children with disabilities were often denied an education solely because of their disabilities. Now, with the addition of laws like the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA), most students with disabilities either spend part or all of their school day in a regular education classroom. While many students with disabilities have benefited from these advancements in law and curriculum, other students with disabilities have not. This discrepancy in the effectiveness of special education is due to the fact that each school district complies with special education laws differently, causing some districts to provide better special education programs than others. This disparity is a direct result of the vaguely-worded special education laws, which leave much room for interpretation. While public schools are supposed to follow the requirements of these laws and provide students with the least restrictive educational environment, the states do little to enforce this. Instead, a school district’s compliance with special education laws is usually driven by outside non-legal actors, such as the parents of those with disabilities, when this should not be the case. Through a case study of the Evanston/Skokie School District 65’s special education plan and through interviews with parents of special needs students in the district, this thesis examines how public schools in Illinois interpret compliance with federal and state special education laws, and how parents as non-legal actors help enforce their districts’ compliance.

title: The Paralyzed Veterans of America: An Ideal Case Study for the Process of Collective Identity
abstract: The roots of the disability rights movement date back to the 1940s, when an obscure group of wounded World War II veterans united over their shared experience to form the Paralyzed Veterans of America (PVA). From its establishment in 1946, the PVA’s immediate goals focused on the interests of its members, paraplegic and quadriplegic veterans. But unlike other veteran organizations of the time, the PVA aligned with disabled civilians and formed a coalition that would mature and expand into a partnership that advocates the rights of all disabled Americans. This study traces the historical development of the PVA and analyzes its progression from a relatively small veterans group into a broad social movement organization. I argue that the transformative experience of the PVA serves as an ideal empirical case study for exploring “collective identity” processes that are necessary for social movements. My historical analysis of the PVA is a unique case study to add to the incomplete scholarship on collective identity. Through tracing the history of the PVA, I illuminate authors’ propositions regarding changes in cohorts and generations, strategies of identity deployment, relations with the state, and legal influences. I argue that these factors are all part of the collective experience of the PVA and impact its actions to invoke broad social change.

title: Treatment of Epileptic Seizures through the Inactivation of GABA-Aminotransferase
abstract: Epilepsy is a chronic neurological disorder characterized by recurrent convulsive seizures that affects over 50 million people, 90% of whom live in developing countries. It is one of the oldest documented diseases, increases a person’s risk for premature death by two to three times, and in America alone has an estimated cost of $15.5 billion/yr. While convulsions can occur for a multitude of reasons, it has been found that an imbalance of the important inhibitory neurotransmitter γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) can cause convulsive seizures. In fact, GABA system malfunction has been associated with the symptoms of Parkinson’s disease, Huntington’s disease, and tardive dyskinesia. An obvious treatment would be to administer GABA to patients; however, GABA itself can’t cross the blood brain barrier, which is a separation of circulating blood and cerebrospinal fluid that restricts the diffusion of large or hydrophilic molecules into the bloodstream. An alternate and more efficient strategy is to design a GABA-like molecule which can cross the blood-brain barrier and inhibit GABA aminotransferase, an enzyme responsible for the degradation of GABA. Vigabatrin, a commercial drug, uses this method of action and has demonstrated efficacy as an antiepileptic drug for refractory complex partial seizures and for infantile spasms. Vigabatrin, however has serious side effects such as visual blurring and constriction of visual fields. My research this past year has focused on investigating novel GABA inhibitors that could treat epilepsy without deleterious side effects.

title: A Break in the Silver Screen: Potentiality and the Metropolitan Encounter in Jean-Luc Godard’s Cinema
abstract: In a 1960s France that was hurtling full speed ahead on the track towards modernity, New Wave filmmaker Jean-Luc Godard realized his first works, attempting to capture the constant movement and unpredictability that characterized the decade. For instance, he would interrupt his main intrigues by inserting documentary-like shots of the streets and crowds of Paris; film anonymous extras in close-up, rivaling the main protagonists’ presence; and drown out dialogue by either overwhelming it through city noises or by cutting sound off all together to create an all-encompassing silence. Consequently, his films not only demonstrated a distinct rupture from the rules that governed classical, narrative cinema, but they also attempted to link together what would appear to be disparate elements and opposing forces. Despite modernity’s overwhelming tendency towards individualism and solitude, Godard yearned to seize the fluid potential at the heart of the metropolitan experience: the notion that we could all possibly be tied to one another; that any seemingly minute encounter could eventually affect society and history; and that we could never have One without taking into consideration the Other. After all, there can be no construction without deconstruction; mobility without immobility; and, above all, no film without a spectator. Cinema, then, if exercised to its fullest potential, could very well break through not only social barriers that normally separate individuals from one another, but also break through its very own barriers, reaching past the screen to directly affect—and possibly even communicate with—its spectator.

title: Malnutrition in Malawi: Non-Governmental Organization Employment of RUTF Products to Address Malnutrition in Malawi
abstract: Malawi is a resource-scarce and food-insecure nation where approximately 70% of children under five suffer from varying degrees of malnutrition, ranging from stunting to severe wasting. The causes of severe acute malnutrition (SAM) are a composite of salient, non-clinical health-related issues rising from a general lack of economic and public-health development, and many malnutrition patients require intensive medical care from skilled staff. Traditional treatment is time-, energy-, and resource-consuming, and places high opportunity costs on mothers of malnourished children in terms of income lost in the process. We sought to examine the use of ready-to-use-food (RUTF) products in conjunction with Community-based Therapeutic Care (CTC) as a more culturally and socioeconomically appropriate and effective approach to malnutrition treatment in rural Malawian communities. Through our interactions with the Malawi Ministry of Health and non-governmental organizations (NGOs), we observed both inpatient and outpatient treatment, and examined each tier of the CTC approach: RUTF production and dispensation, management of outpatient distribution sites, training among aid workers and education amongst villagers regarding appropriate nutritional health and RUTF use. In doing so, we learned about the collaboration and lines of communication between the Malawi Ministry of Health and supporting NGOs, the challenges faced, and lessons learned in their efforts to combat malnutrition.

title: Processing Newly-Learned Verbs: Evidence from Toddlers
abstract: To acquire a new verb’s meaning, toddlers use the verb’s syntactic context along with observation of a referential scene. But acquiring a new verb also requires integrating its representation into the parsing machinery. The current study (a) demonstrates that 21-month-old toddlers infer a novel verb’s meaning from syntactic context even in the absence of a referential scene and (b) sheds light on how quickly toddlers process the novel verb and orient their attention toward its referent once candidate events are displayed. We exposed forty toddlers (average 21.21 months) to novel verbs. Toddlers first watched a two-actor conversation featuring a novel verb in either Transitive or Intransitive sentences. They then viewed two side-by-side videos: a causative action and a synchronous action. After a baseline period, during which no novel word was presented, toddlers heard, e.g., “Where’s mooping?” We analyzed the time-course of toddlers’ looking to determine when looking patterns in the two conditions began to diverge. In the baseline period, looking patterns did not differ across conditions. But 2.5 secs after the onset of the novel word in the question “Where’s mooping?”, toddlers in the Transitive condition reliably preferred the causative scene compared to toddlers in the Intransitive condition, (t(40)=2.8898, p=.0063).

title: "Eating Bitterness”: A Comparative Analysis of State and UNICEF Policies for Left-Behind Children in China
abstract: The left-behind children of rural China are a devastating phenomenon. Migrant parents are often forced to either “take their children to the cities and subject them to institutionalized discrimination, or leave them behind in the countryside in the uncertain care of relatives.” Often migrant parents choose the latter. The China Daily estimates that approximately 58 million left-behind children live in the countryside today, with 40 million under the age of 14. More than 53% of these children have no direct parental care. This population of children is subjected to social, psychological, and emotional pain. Furthermore, they are not receiving a proper education. This latter point is especially interesting since the government of China considers its education system critical to future economic growth. This paper analyzes the educational initiatives of the Chinese government and UNICEF. Both initiatives have differing outcomes. I propose the differences are due to institutionalism, as defined by Keohane: institutions make a significant difference in conjunction with power realities. Most importantly, institutions have an interactive effect, meaning that their impact on outcomes varies, depending on the nature of power and interests. However, the institutional structure of the organizations leads to the differing outcomes in educating left-behind children. In this paper, I define success as secondary enrollment. Based on the variable of secondary enrollment, I will demonstrate that UNICEF is more successful in addressing the problem of educating the left-behind children population.

title: Beyond Ballet: Uncovering Social Processes in a Chicago Dance Studio
abstract: This study examined the social processes that occur during a Creative Movement dance class at a Chicago dance studio. This research used a case study approach to closely examine the selected Creative Movement class and its specific population of female students, ages three to four years, their parents, and the teacher. The researcher assumed the position of the class’s assistant teacher and used participant observation to examine the social interaction in order to develop a better understanding of a dance studio’s functions and purposes beyond dance education. An analytical and theoretical framework of structural functionalism, symbolic interactionism, and social behaviorism exposed three social processes: self-development, socialization, and group formation. The findings also emphasized the significance of the instructor’s personality and teaching philosophy. Overall, this study discourages society’s dismissal of the dance studio as solely a place where little girls learn how to move and encourages the perspective that the studio is an educational institution where the social processes of socialization and child development occur and a vital sense of community is established.

title: Enantioselective Total Synthesis of Streptorubin B
abstract: Streptorubin B is a bacterially-derived natural product with promising antimalarial and other biological activities. The inefficiency of acquisition of the natural product, as well as interest in totally synthetic derivatives thereof, prompted our research into the development of a chemical synthesis of the naturally-occurring molecule. The enantioselective total synthesis of streptorubin B is herein described, with key steps en route to the natural product including a one-pot organocatalytic intramolecular aldol-Wittig reaction, an oxy-anion Cope rearrangement, and a biomimetic condensation. Synthetic streptorubin B was attained in ca. 9% yield over 9 steps as a single atrop-diastereomer and as a ca. 98:2 mixture of enantiomers. Structure features unique to streptorubin B among the prodigiosin alkaloid family were uncovered and are herein disclosed.

title: Bioavailability of Mercury in Aquatic Systems
abstract: Inorganic mercury is released directly and indirectly to the environments as part of several industrial processes such as coal burning. In the natural environment, anaerobic organisms in aquatic systems transform the inorganic mercury to methylmercury through a process called methylation. Methylmercury is a toxin that bioaccumulates in the aquatic food chain, with high concentrations found in many species of fish that humans consume. Ingested methylmercury is readily and completely absorbed by the gastrointestinal tract and transported across the blood-brain barrier and the placenta. Therefore, from both and environmental and public health perspective, this organometallic compound has become an alarming pollutant. In order for methylation to occur, inorganic mercury must first be bioavailable—able to enter a cell by passing through the cell membrane. Our research investigates how the bioavailability of mercury changes in the presence of various anthropogenic ligands and natural complexants, including ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid, nitrilotriacetic acid, cysteine, humic acid, and citrate. Bioavailability was measured via bioluminescence assays performed on a genetically engineered whole cell mercury bioreporter (Escherichia.Coli ARL1 with merR::luxCDABE fusion). Our results show that cellular mercury uptake is greatly enhanced in the presence of the amino acid cysteine (10-2 μM – 10-4 μM levels), suggesting that a mercury-cysteine complex forms to facilitate the cross-membrane transfer. Meanwhile, mercury uptake is greatly inhibited in the presence of citrate (10-2 μM levels). Therefore, because the bioavailability of mercury changes by complexing to ligands, microbial methylations of mercury will strongly depend on the composition and quality of an aquatic system.

title: The Impact of Spirituality and Self-Concept on Quality of Life for Cancer Patients
abstract: Efforts toward understanding how cancer affects individuals in a holistic way has led to increased research on psychosocial variables which may impact patients’ quality of life (QOL) post-diagnosis. The sample used in this study was taken from the Cancer Supplement to the National Institutes of Health Patient Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) Initiative. Participants (N = 509) were cancer patients recruited from Chicagoland oncology clinics or local and national support societies. They were asked to endorse statements regarding their level of spirituality and self-concept before and after diagnosis, and then to recall what that level was pre-diagnosis. Spirituality and self-concept were determined using PROMIS negative illness impact items and short forms. QOL was determined based on the Global Short Form. Statistical analyses were used to evaluate the individual and combined impacts of spirituality and self-concept on patients’ QOL post-cancer diagnosis. Results showed that spirituality and self-concept each increased after diagnosis. Spirituality pre-diagnosis and self-concept pre-diagnosis each significantly predicted QOL. Finally, spirituality and self-concept pre-diagnosis demonstrated an interactive effect on QOL in that participants with the highest spirituality and highest self-esteem had the highest QOL. Understanding how QOL is affected by spirituality and self-concept before and after a cancer diagnosis may be useful in creating therapeutic interventions that help reduce the psychosocial burden of cancer.

title: The Intersection of Vision, Language, and Space
abstract: Making sense of the visual world is a complicated task not only because we must recognize a vast number of objects within our field of view, but also because we must recognize the spatial arrangement among them. There are two ways that we might perceive spatial relations between objects in our field of view. We might encode both objects at once like the simultaneous notes of a musical chord. Another possibility is that we might use shifts of attention to process the objects one by one, in a sequence over time, like a series of notes. Because eye gaze location corresponds to where attention is being allocated, we used eye tracking to explore the spontaneous eye movement patterns that arise when people are encoding spatial relations. When presented with two colored dots, participants tend to systematically make their initial eye movements to the left. However, this tendency only appears when the task requires encoding the spatial relation; in a non-spatial task, this leftward preference disappears. In another experiment, before seeing two colored dots, participants were first prompted with questions regarding their spatial relation (e.g. Is red left of green?). The data reveal that participants’ saccade patterns are guided by both the first color in the question (red or green) and the direction term used (left or right). These data suggest that extracting spatial relations involves processing the objects sequentially.

title: Contemporary Religion as Practical Identity
abstract: Religious phenomena – meaning, the beliefs and actions of religious adherents – are the products of each individual adherent’s religious practical identity. An individual’s practical identity (a term borrowed from philosopher Christine Korsgaard) is a description on which a self-reflective agent values her/himself and by which an agent gives her/himself obligations for belief and action. In this article, I argue that any agent’s “religion” can only be defined as one among her/his practical identities. Furthermore, I argue that “religion” cannot be defined as an entity that exists as anything other than a specific type of practical identity. Religious practical identities are distinguishable from nonreligious practical identities because of the adherents’ belief in (that is, valuation of themselves in relation to) the supernatural. In this way, religious phenomena are seen to be expressions of the adherents’ values by means of their religious practical identities.

title: The Scientific Gender Gap: Gender Bias in Facial Inferences that Predict Scientific Influence
abstract: Although the number of female scientists earning graduate degrees in science, technology, engineering and math (STEM) fields has increased steadily in the past 15 years, the gender gap in higher echelons of science has remained. What psychological factors underlie the scientific gender gap at the highest levels of STEM fields? From politics to business, facial appearance has been shown to play a pivotal role in predicting an individual’s success. In this study we examined the possibility that facial appearance may contribute to scientific success and, in particular, to a gender gap in scientific influence as measured by h index. Sixty Caucasian American undergraduate students viewed 110 grayscale facial photographs (55 females) of professors at the top five STEM departments. Participants viewed each face for a brief moment and rated how approachable, attractive, competent, and dominant the face seemed on a 7-point scale. Across all faces, scientific age (year of PhD) was a positive predictor of h index. For female scientists, perceived approachability and dominance of facial appearance were negative predictors of h index, whereas for male scientists, facial inferences did not predict scientific influence—there were no significant predictors of facial appearance in predicting h index for men. The follow-up study revealed that the significant predictors of scientific influence for female professors observed in the initial study were unique to the scientists at the top five institutions. These results indicate that shallow decision heuristics, such as trait inferences made from the face, play an important role in scientific influence and may contribute to the perseverance of gender gap at the highest levels of STEM fields.

title: Regulation of the Heat Shock Response by Tissue-Specific Networks in Caenorhabditis elegans
abstract: The long term health of the cell is inseparably linked with protein homeostasis, which is maintained by a highly complex network of molecular interactions that balance essential biological pathways such as protein synthesis, folding, degradation, and transport. However, to adapt and restore any imbalances in protein homeostasis, the heat shock response (HSR) coordinates activities of protective stress response pathways, which involves the activation of heat shock factor-1 (HSF-1), a transcription factor repressed in the absence of stress by the Hsp70 and Hsp90 molecular chaperones. Although specific components of the HSR are well understood at the cellular level, little is known about its regulations in the context of an intact, multicellular organism. Therefore, a genome-wide RNAi screen was performed to identify negative regulators of the HSR, termed heat shock inhibitors (HSIs), using a stress-inducible reporter pHsp70::GFP in the absence of exogenous stress. Due to the frequent appearance of false negatives, I took the results of the primary screen and performed a candidate approach to identify and characterize additional HSIs using a more sensitive detection method. First, I pursued a functional approach to screen all genes that are subunits or members of major complexes/classes in protein homeostasis. Second, network analysis shows tissue specific interaction among the HSIs. Therefore, in addition to the functional approach, I pursued an interaction approach by screening genes that interact with HSIs identified in the genome-wide screen. In total, we identified 55 genes that repress pHsp70::GFP expression in an HSF-1 dependent manner.

title: The Synthesis and Characterization of a β-galactosidase Activateable MRI Contrast Agent
abstract: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) allows tomographic, temporal, and non-invasive imaging without the use of ionizing radiation. Whereas the primary drawback of MRI is its decreased sensitivity as compared to other techniques, contrast agents can serve to enhance resolution. The focus of this project is the synthesis and characterization of an MRI contrast agent that responds to the presence of β-galactosidase, the enzyme commonly encoded for by the reporter gene lac z. Such an agent could be used to follow gene expression throughout an experimental organism over time by MRI. Two obstacles currently hinder the success of these agents: poor cellular uptake and slow enzymatic cleavage. This research is focused on improving enzyme kinetics through the synthesis of an agent based on a self-immolative mechanism precedented by drug delivery systems. The chemical synthesis of several successfully synthesized agents will be described, as well as their respective characterization data obtained from relaxivity assays, enzyme kinetic tests, and cell studies. The in vitro enzyme kinetic data suggests that the synthesized agents will cleave on an MRI-relevant timescale. However, initial relaxivity tests demonstrate an unfavorable relaxivity change for the synthesized agents, though this must be explored in vivo. These shortcomings will hopefully be overcome in a revised target compound that combines fast enzymatic cleavage characteristics with the structure of a Zn2+-activated agent that has demonstrated a favorable relaxivity change. If successful, the synthesis and characterization of a β-galactosidase activateable MRI contrast agent would represent a potentially revolutionary advance for biological research.

title: Spanish-Speakers’ Understanding, Behavior, and Use of Prescription Medicine When Confronted with the Language-Barrier
abstract: Research has shown that over half of pharmacies in the United States lack Spanish translation services for medicine not available over the counter. This research aims to investigate pharmaceutical drug usage of the Spanish-speaking community when English proficiency is limited. As the population of Spanish-speakers in the United States continues to increase, the need for health literacy is necessary in order to improve public health. This study will involve approximately 50 Spanish-speaking subjects, who will be questioned about their behavior regarding pharmaceutical usage. This research will survey Spanish-speaking respondents about their experiences with pharmaceuticals and the availability of translation services in their pharmacy interactions to find out more about the need for better linguistic services in US pharmacies.

title: The Post-Capitalist Turn: Feminist Materialism and Subcultural Politics
abstract: My senior thesis for the Gender Studies program focuses on the political dimensions of subcultural style, identity, and daily practices. Focusing specifically on Latino punk bands from the South-side of Chicago, the research spans a variety of approaches: from modern radical political theories of the 1960s, to the genesis of cultural studies in academia during the mid- and late-1970s, to the ideas of contemporary feminist materialists who problematize many of the assumptions previous authors and activists have made about cultural politics in general and the political potentialities of punk subcultures specifically. The research project aims to activate feminist and cultural theory in order to construct alternate modes of organization for the contemporary radical left that embrace a continuum between the personal and the political, rather than sacrificing one for the other. The specific case of Chicago’s Latino punk community provides an excellent model for exploring these questions of identity, politics, and economic subjectivity. This community’s practices break significantly from both traditional leftist ideology as well as commonly held assumptions about subcultural functions. Their nuanced navigations of both individual autonomy and collective solidarity appear to support the revelations of materialist feminists and cultural theorists alike, and could potentially offer radical new political subjectivities as cultural tactics for the confrontation of neoliberal capitalism as it manifests in everyday urban life.

title: In Their Own Words: Minority Youth Experiences at a Charter High School
abstract: Charter schools are autonomous public schools that some observers and policy makers view as a viable solution in current education reform efforts. As it relates to measures of student performance, research on charter schools and their ability to raise students’ test scores at the high school level has been mixed. Despite this mixed research, charter schools are still often lauded as schools in which minority (African American and Latino/a) youth can receive a quality education. However African American and Latino/a youths own understanding of their respective school’s culture and how that culture influences their attitudes towards schooling and academic achievement has not been extensively studied. This qualitative study seeks to understand how African American and Latino/a students contextualize their schooling experiences at Jackson College Prep charter high school as it specifically relates to the school culture’s impact on their attitudes towards schooling and academic achievement. Understanding these experiences from the perspective of the students themselves provides observers and policy makers with more information from important stakeholders—students—and introduces an additional criterion by which the effectiveness of charter schools in providing students with transformative educational opportunities can be judged.

title: Characterization of Synapses on the Basal Dendrites of Hippocampal CA1 Neurons
abstract: The hippocampus is a brain structure implicated in learning and memory consolidation, and damage to this region has been shown to impair the ability to form new memories. However, the neuronal connections that form the basis of learning and memory mechanisms have not been fully elucidated. A single neuron in the hippocampus may receive input from hundreds of other cells via synapses, confirming that these sub-micron-scale connections are important in interneuronal communication. We seek to understand the properties of synapses and signal integration in the dendrites of hippocampal CA1 pyramidal neurons. The basal and apical dendrites of these cells have distinct morphologies, suggesting that there may be functional differences in the mechanisms that each utilizes for synaptic signal integration. Previous studies show that synapses in the apical dendritic region exhibit distance-dependent scaling of strength, characterized by the scaling of synapse size and of glutamate receptor expression. Through the use of serial-section conventional and immunogold electron microscopy, we characterized synapses in the basal dendritic region based on size, type, and density of AMPA-type and NMDA-type glutamate receptors. Our results indicate that the basal dendrites do utilize different methods of synaptic signal integration. These findings suggest that differences in morphology of the two dendritic arbors may result in differences in the dendritic mechanisms of information processing.

title: Percolations in Complex Networks
abstract: In our globalized world, the magnitude and intensity of modern human traffic has made human society more susceptible to threats intimately connected to human travel, with the recent spreading of H1N1 Influenza in 2009 being a prime example of a modern epidemic. Therefore, the understanding of human mobility and the development of qualitative models as well as quantitative theories for it is of key importance to the research of human infectious disease dynamics on large geographical scales. This project investigates the stability of multi-scale human transportation networks in response to the removal of nodes and links, in particular, the percolation threshold for the US human mobility network. It examines the type of links and nodes that are important for the structural integrity of the networks, and whether long range (weaker) interactions play a more significant role in spatial disease dynamics. The data for the multi-scale human mobility networks is generated based on a proxy network of dispersing US dollar bills.

title: Inverse Relationship Between Infancy Breastfeeding and Adulthood T2D Risk in Males: A Filipino Case Study
abstract: The most prevalent diseases in the world today fall into one of two categories: infectious or chronic. An infant’s susceptibility to infectious disease has been shown to be somewhat lessened via breast milk exposure. Is it possible that breastfeeding could also lessen susceptibility to future chronic disease? Specifically, does breastfeeding “program” some level of resistance against adulthood Type 2 Diabetes (T2D)? Using data gathered from the Cebu Longitudinal Health and Nutrition Survey (CLHNS), this study examines breastfeeding both in terms of intensity (n=989) and duration (n=993). Intensity is a 3-part categorical variable: exclusively breastfed, exclusively formula fed, or mixed. Duration is defined in terms of quartiles of days breastfed. The T2D risk factors are fed insulin (μg/mL), BMI (kg/m2), and waist circumference (cm). In women, we found no relationship between breast milk exposure and T2D risk factors. In men, however, we found significant (P ≤ 0.01) inverse dose-response relationships between infancy breastfeeding and adulthood fed insulin level. This relationship exists when analyzing intensity of breastfeeding as well as when analyzing duration of breastfeeding – even when controlling for adulthood BMI and waist circumference. These results show that breastfeeding not only protects against infectious disease: it can also reduce future susceptibility to a chronic disease, T2D.

title: Preferences for Causal Information in 3-4 Year Old Children
abstract: There has been much debate in recent years regarding whether or not causal information is influential in helping children to remember the names of objects. It is unclear as to whether this causal information merely draws a children's attention to the objects, making children more cognizant, able to remember these objects names. Dr. Amy Booth (2009) explored this concept in three- to four-year-old children by presenting them with novel objects with given descriptions which had causal, noncausal, or baseline information. Results showed that children retained more information about causal objects after a delay period. The current study looks to find if after presenting children with objects, they tend to have a preference for objects presented with causal information or not,. This will be done by allowing the child to choose which object they would like to hear more about. It is hypothesized that if causal information is more interesting, children will be more likely to want to hear more about causal objects. If it is not more interesting, they will choose to hear about all objects equally. Data is currently being analyzed.

title: Navigating the "Tangle of Pathology": Community Organization and Family Strength in Watts on the Eve of the 1965 Rebellion
abstract: During the 1965 Watts rebellion, blacks from Los Angeles looted local businesses, torched buildings, and fought with police officers. The urban violence was a reaction to the political, social, and economic injustices that racialized, white American attitudes had produced. The participants viewed their acts as the only means through which they could express their discontent; the community’s political marginalization denied the residents any other meaningful avenues through which they could articulate their grievances. But as journalists and government officials struggled to understand the rebellion, they failed to recognize its social and political impetus. Through the lens of racial stereotypes and literature on the “culture of poverty,” whites—and some blacks—viewed the rebellion as a meaningless “riot.” It was the product of the social pathologies that social scientists believed to be endemic in black urban “ghettos.” Journalistic accounts and official reports indicated that community disorganization, emasculation and shiftlessness of black males, and single-mother households had destabilized the region. In my research, however, I have found evidence of extensive political and social organization within Watts on the eve of the rebellion. While past scholarship has explored the political meaning behind the rebellion, my work identifies the sources of communal strength that sustained residents in and around Watts. Through exploring the mechanisms that helped blacks cope with their daily socioeconomic struggles, I argue that the rebellion emerged not from an area where poor leadership and broken homes had produced a riot-prone youth, but rather occurred in a cohesive and self-supporting community.

title: Toubab Shift: Identifying Socially Salient Factors of Legitimization and Differentiation
abstract: An obvious reference to a foreigner in a market or walking along the busy streets of Dakar, Senegal, the word toubab is a marker of interracial interaction and an open door that brings the black and white histories of Senegal to the forefront. It is just one instance of local language use that expresses identity and belonging in a contested space consructed and transformed through colonization. 'Toubab' indexes shifting identities and conceptions of the interlocutors and signifies situational relationships between them. My research shows that there are several accepted and still socially contested meanings of the term that reflect specific salient evaluating characteristics. I argue that these characteristics can be organized as instances of asserting agency and identity, drawing comparisons or borders, and defining legitimacy between individuals. These characteristics allow the term to function in multiple settings because of emphasis placed on social distance between both groups (ie. French and Senegalese) and specific individuals (ie. two Senegalese). The term’s usage reifies borders creating outsiders and insiders, defining legitimate and acceptable individuals and practices among foreigners as well as other Senegalese. The people of a country still under the influence of French rule are creating a border between an 'authentic' culture standard and western practice and culture through its use. My research and analysis explores the cross section of language use, boundary formation, and contested colonizer legitimacy that has been rarely interrogated from the perspective of the delegitimized population. I looked at the perceptions, social contexts, and historical contexts of Senegal surrounding these interactions and reinforcing Senegalese identity as separate from French influenced. The unique context of Senegal will shed light on the ways in which identity and legitimization are not always as clear as previously postulated in places of black majority and white hegemony.

title: Motherland
abstract: “Motherland” is a collection of essays that circles a uniquely American theme: the problem of mixed inheritance. When I realized I’d be writing into a tradition of memoirs about ethnic difference, I was determined to shun questions of identity politics. This is partly because such questions had already been thoroughly canvassed by earlier writers. Memoirists Maxine Hong Kingston and Theresa Hak Kyung Cha shaped the genre for Asian Americans decades ago, and their works meditate on themes of placelessness and alienation. Their books are artful, but also sometimes oddly sociological, as if the authors felt the need to justify their work by the fact of their race. This, I think, is the problem with dwelling on identity politics in creative work: it renders one’s race, one’s inheritance—things as basic as breathing—into something obscure and academic. What this manuscript offers is different. As the daughter of a Chinese immigrant and a white American, I was born into two worlds, neither of which I could claim. But I never felt tortured or grieved by this, was never plagued by questions of identity. What interested me was something more basic and perhaps more brutal: the necessary betrayals that immigrants and their children must make in order to claim their dignity as Americans. For my mother, this meant a betrayal of the place she came from, her motherland. For me, as the last essay in the collection suggests, it may mean a betrayal of my own mother, the land I come from.

title: Numerical Processing of Mathematical Functions
abstract: Much exploration is needed in the realm of understanding mathematical processing, especially in order to develop remediation techniques for math disabilities. In the present functional magnetic resonance (fMRI) experiment, subjects were presented with four different tasks: a non-symbolic quantity comparison task (numerosity), a language task, a subtraction task, and a multiplication task. The current existing knowledge on the neural pathways involved in math processing says that numerosity activates regions in the right horizontal intraparietal sulcus (IPS), and rhyming and language tasks recruit temporal and frontal region. From this, I developed the hypothesis that there will be an overlap between the activation of regions involved in the quantity comparison and subtraction tasks in the IPS, and between the regions involved in the language and multiplication tasks in the left IFG and middle temporal gyrus (MTG). Furthermore, those individuals who have robust activity in the regions involved in quantity comparison and rhyming should also have strong recruitment of these areas in subtraction and multiplication, respectively. This is one of the first studies, to my knowledge, that is exploring both language and mathematical computations within the same sub-set population of subjects.

title: Krumping and Voguing as a Means to an End: A New Outlook on Dance, Identity Politics, the Creation of Safe Space & the Transformative Politics of Spirituality
abstract: Dance as a vessel of communication has been used in various ways. From social commentary to social protest, it has evolved into a multifaceted approach to raise questions that society doesn’t want to answer, and re-define the hegemonies that are seemingly etched in stone. But what happens when dance leaves the concert stage with orchestras and, instead, takes place in a circle of spectators in the streets of South Central, or in a gymnasium in Chicago rented for a gay ball? Most importantly, how does dance impact a culture where pain, poverty, and oppression are everyday affairs and happiness can only be found on the dance floor? In my analysis of Krumping and Voguing, I reveal that dance not only functions as a form of healing and social protest, but also as a source of protection through kinship structures as an alternative to gang affiliation. These forms both reconfigure Black masculinity and Identity politics, showing the importance of creating a safe space of expression where dance becomes a transformative spiritual experience through ritualistic performance. Krumping and Voguing reveal the importance of subcultural identity and the importance of “cool,” the performative aesthetic of “cool” and the continuum of masculinity in Black culture. This research is incredibly significant because there is no academic literature utilizing Voguing as a means to understand Krumping or even comparing the two. Although they appear to be polar opposites, my research proves that they are more similar than we care to admit.

title: Mexican-American Agency: The Shrunken Head of Pancho Villa's Influence upon Mexican-American Identity
abstract: Perceptions of the representation of Pancho Villa’s personality, physical appearance and actions during the Mexican revolution have inspired Mexican-Americans to reproduce his persona in corridos, stories, pictures and other cultural mediums. Simply put, stories about the historical figure of Pancho Villa have shaped the childhood and identities of Mexican-American immigrants in the United States. Although, Francisco “Pancho” Villa was a real character of the Mexican Revolution in 1910, he has become a mythical figure that represents border culture and expresses contemporary Mexican-American identity. In this project, I will utilize Luis Valdez’s play The Shrunken Head of Pancho Villa to analyze its impact upon Mexican-American identity in the United States. The Shrunken Head of Pancho Villa not only embodies Mexican-American history in the United States; it also presents the dichotomies between Mexican-American collective memory of Mexico and the disconnected reality of life in the United States. In the play, the characters of Belarmino, Domingo and Joaquin represent different Mexican-American identities. Belarmino is a floating head, that of Pancho Villa, symbolizing the Mexican past. By selecting this play, I seek to understand how stories can be employed to mobilize and politically unify Mexican-Americans today. More importantly, storytelling gives individuals a history; it revives past events and utilizes them in the present. That being said, how can Mexican-Americans change our narrative in the United States? It is my belief that the answer to this question will influence the political, cultural and economic future of Mexicans and Mexican-Americans in the United States.

title: Blogging to Democracy in Iran: Political Memory and the Role of the Bazaar
abstract: My research explores the role of blogs in the current reform movement in Iran, which began in June 2009 in protest of fraudulent elections. Many predict that this movement may evolve into a revolution reminiscent of 1979 and may even serve as the catalyst to democratize Iran. They cite the Internet, particularly blogs, as an unprecedented means of expression under an oppressive regime. To serve as a gateway into understanding the potential influence of blogs in Iranian politics, I explore how blogs have influenced the political memory and national identity of two key events in Iran's recent history, the 1953 coup and the Revolution of 1978-1979. I also evaluate the role of mass media and technology in these key events as a framework for understanding the potential force of blogs today. I conclude that although blogs are transforming the way in which Iranians are communicating and challenging the current regime, they are limited in scope due to censorship and restricted accessibility. Moreover, I argue that in order to induce significant political change in Iran, it is essential that traditional channels of communication like bazaars be utilized in conjunction with high-tech modes of communication like blogs.

title: Glycogen Synthase Kinase 3 beta (GSK3β) Inhibitors Block Cell Growth and Induce Apoptosis in Ovarian Cancer Cells
abstract: Ovarian cancer is the most lethal gynecological malignancy among US women. Combination therapy or alternative strategies are of great importance. A possible target is glycogen synthase kinase 3β (GSK3β), which is a protein that is overexpressed in serous ovarian cancer. Recent studies have shown that GSK3β inhibitors (GSKi) are known to induce apoptosis in pancreatic cancer cells, and can destabilize p53, which may promote cellular death in response to DNA damaging agents, much like chemotherapy. Inhibitors of GSK3β, a downstream kinase in the Wnt signaling pathway, were evaluated as a probable drug therapy using serous ovarian cancer cell lines. A series of GSK3β inhibitors were synthesized and then tested in vivo and in vitro using SKOV3 and OVCA432 ovarian cancer cell lines. 9ING41, which was found the most effective, induced apoptosis as indicated by DAPI positive nuclear condensation, PARP cleavage, and TUNEL analysis. Activation of caspase-3, as depicted using western blot analysis on ovarian cancer cells, indicated that the mechanism for apoptosis involves caspase activation. Additionally, GSKi significantly downregulated phosphorylation of the α and β subunits of GSK in the OVCA432 cell line, reduced levels of cyclinD1, and inhibited phosphorylation of downstream target glycogen synthase. An in vivo xenograft study using SKOV3 cells demonstrated that tumor progression was hindered by 9ING41 in vivo and phosphorylation of downstream molecules including the β subunit of GSK and phosphorylated glycogen synthase were blocked. Therefore, GSK3β inhibitors alone or in combination with existing drugs may provide an alternative treatment strategy to serous ovarian cancers.

title: The Good Life
abstract: Throughout the 2008-2009 academic year, I researched Bill Clinton's presidency, focusing primarily on his relationship with Monica Lewinsky. I was interested in examining the scandal because it was the only instance in my lifetime where I could see the nation's highest office-holder as a human being rather than just a politician. I used this research to write a creative nonfiction essay where I paralleled Clinton's experiences with Monica Lewinsky with my own adolescent experiences with my first girlfriend. The essay works partially as a coming-of-age piece, with themes of sexual awakening and its consequences; yet, in the context of the Lewinsky Scandal, the piece also illustrates a relevant, personal connection between unlikely sources -- a teenager and the President of the United States. In doing so, the essay demonstrates the universality of sexual and romantic confusion.

title: 教 (Jiao)
abstract: "教 (Jiao)" is a work of historical fiction based on the Chinese Educational Mission to Hartford, Connecticut in 1872. In 1872 the Chinese government, reeling from losses in the Opium Wars, approved a mission of 120 students to study science and technology in the United States. The students studied in the U.S. for nine years before returning to China to aid in its modernization. "教 (Jiao)" takes place at the very beginning of the students' time in America, exploring the painful choice they faced between the seductions of American culture and their loyalty to the mission, China, and each other. In preparation for writing this story, I conducted original historical research in the Connecticut Historical Society archives. I examined local newspapers, letters, journals, photographs, drawings, and cultural artifacts. In addition to these archival materials, I relied on memoirs by Chinese officials, Chinese students, and their American hosts. Besides historical research, I researched the etymology of several Chinese characters featured in the stories. I examined the subtle connotations conferred on the characters by their pictographic origins. The small historical literature on the Chinese Educational Mission tends to treat the mission as a vehicle of China's modernization rather than as an early Chinese-American cultural exchange. In "教 (Jiao)," I use the medium of historical fiction to more richly explore the painful process of cultural exchange that underlay Chinese Educational Mission.

title: Reverberations and Reflections: A Case Study of The Philadelphia Freedom Schools
abstract: Through a case study of The Philadelphia Freedom Schools, this project examines the role of educational philosophy in the African historical experience, emphasizing the schools’ improvisational adaptation of select cultural texts and practices from the model introduced by the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee’s (SNCC) Freedom Schools. Each era’s Freedom Schools offered children an alternative summer education and a parallel educational structure. This structure, employing an African American centered curriculum to emphasize an intergenerational transmission of skills, values and content, critiqued and questioned American society. This study will utilize a qualitative normative Africana Studies theoretical approach to identify the enduring operational intellectual skills and values which transcend time and space. After identifying how this grassroots cultural educational structure, curriculum and process remains apparent in the Philadelphia Freedom Schools, this project suggests the implications of Freedom Schools as a continued means to remedy educational disparities and empower African American communities.

title: Network Destabilizations with Negative Mechanical Responses
abstract: When a system is exposed to slowly changing external forces, we can often approximate its reaction by assuming that it remains near equilibrium throughout its evolution. These so-called quasistatic assumptions, which greatly simplify calculations, often result in very accurate models. However, under some conditions, quasistatic assumptions can fail entirely, and a system can undergo sudden changes, even when exposed to slowly changing conditions. Such destabilizations are often associated with a structural failures and undesired behavior. We explore the use of destabilizations to design systems with unexpected and novel behavior. We consider a solid material composed of a network of interacting particles on which an external normal force is exerted. When this force changes, we expect a deformation to result in the direction of the change in applied force. We have shown that, whenever quasistatic approximations are valid, this intuition holds. However, we have also successfully designed a network which undergoes a destabilization due to a change in the applied force such that when the system regains equilibrium, the deformation of the network from its initial configuration is opposite the direction of the change in force. This response is novel and has not been characterized before. From a materials perspective, this destabilization is manifested as a solid-to-solid, stress induced phase transition. A potential application is the construction of new materials which expand under compression or contract under tension.

title: A Culture of Cooperativism: Female Empowerment and Community Solidarity in the Villa Soberana barrio
abstract: Among scholars of community development, there is an emerging focus on the “culture of cooperativism” that exists within worker cooperatives governed by principles of local worker solidarity and equal ownership. Two such cooperatives, located in Nicaragua’s Nueva Vida barrio and predominantly run by women, are an industrial sewing factory called The Fair Trade Zone and Genesis, a spinning plant cooperative which is currently undergoing construction to provide a consistent supply of organic cloth to The Fair Trade Zone. This study examines to what extent the unique culture of cooperativism within The Fair Trade Zone and Genesis transcends the economic sphere, contributing to a greater feeling of solidarity and empowerment among women of the Nueva Vida barrio. How the worker-owners understand cooperativism and apply it to their lives outside of the workplace was examined through interviews during two stages of cooperative development: the ‘construction stage’ (Genesis) and the ‘completed stage’ (The Fair Trade Zone). This research advances the existing body of knowledge on the emergence of cooperative culture and leads to a greater understanding of how the cooperative model can be applied outside of the workplace to provide motivation for women’s activism in their local communities.

title: The Influence of Geographical Software on Education and Spatial Ability
abstract: Spatial thinking involves the representation and transformation of the locations of objects and figures. The present study investigated the relations between GIS learning and children’s spatial ability by analyzing performance on spatial-related skills tests, and the role of spontaneous gesture in spatial cognition and communication. Participants completed spatial- and content-related tests, a learning phase, and a verbal interview. Ten students were randomly assigned to the experimental condition, in which they used a GIS system, My World; the other ten students were in the control condition and used traditional tables and figures. Students who received GIS training improved more on the post-test than those who received paper and pencil training. Correlation test revealed a positive relationship between amount of spontaneous gesturing and prior knowledge, which can be indicative of the fact that children who have a better understanding of the topic have better mental representations of the spatial concepts, and thus gesture more. Gesture might play a more direct role in the learning process by allowing children to explore - perhaps with less effort - ideas that may be difficult or inappropriate to think through in a verbal format. Malleability of spatial cognition suggests that spatial learning can be fostered by technology and education. Classroom implementation of GIS learning has a great potential to completely restructure the way science is taught in the classroom.

title: Foreign-Born Hispanic Senior Citizens' Perceptions of Aging and Quality of Life in Later Life
abstract: Foreign-born Hispanic senior citizens’ aging experiences display the national need for more culturally competent elder resources for this growing minority population over the age of sixty. Previous research discusses both the immigration experiences and the process of aging among Hispanics living in the United States, yet these fields of research currently remain disconnected. My interviews with twenty Mexican and Puerto Rican senior citizens participating at Milwaukee’s United Community Center’s (UCC) Senior Center tie together the research on immigration and the research on aging. The interviews focus on the seniors’ immigration experiences, level of acculturation, reasons for participating at the Senior Center and satisfaction with their older life. I consider their responses according to their birth place, time spent living in the United States, reasons for immigration and language use. Bicultural senior centers, like the UCC’s Senior Center, present Hispanic elders with an opportunity to remain independent, engage in diverse activities and practice their heritage culture. Despite their heterogeneous immigration stories and cultural values, all twenty seniors view their experiences at the Senior Center positively, with many explicitly crediting the Center with improving their quality of life. Therefore, more senior centers should model themselves after the UCC’s Senior Center by offering programming created with the particular needs of their clients in mind in order to provide the elderly with more valuable resources. My discussion of the immigrant experience with American elder care also illuminates other national issues, especially the roles of minority status and bilingualism in determining access to healthcare.

title: Characterization of MicroRNA Expression in Urinary Bladder Neural Cells of Pediatric Patients Afflicted with Spina Bifida
abstract: Neural tube defects are the most common incapacitating birth defects in the United States. These defects include defects of the brain (anencephaly), but are mostly defects of the spine (spina bifida). Spina bifida is caused by the failure of the neural tube to close during the first month of embryonic development. When the spinal cord itself is not fully formed, the nerves do not develop as they should and the growing fetus develops myelomeningocele (MM). The most severe form of spina bifida, MM manifests itself in the form of a physical opening from a range of the lower thoracic to sacral regions of the spinal column, exposing the nerves and the meninges. The exposed nerves located at the sacral level of the spinal column control bowel and bladder function and must be surgically repositioned into the body, typically immediately after birth. Hence, almost all individuals with spina bifida have bowel and bladder dysfunction resulting in a neurogenic bladder. Patients with a neurogenic bladder may also suffer from urinary tract infections, hemorrhagic cystitis, pyelonephritis, epididymitis or stone disease.
